meanings_ja: n. 領事
definition_en: an official sent to live in a foreign city to help and protect citizens of their own country
example1_en: The consul helped us after we lost our passports.
example1_ja: パスポートをなくしたとき、領事が助けてくれた。
example2_en: A consul may support citizens facing difficulties overseas and help strengthen commercial links between countries.
example2_ja: 領事は、海外で困っている自国民を支援し、国同士の商業的なつながりを強める役割を担うことがある。
collocations: consul general｜総領事 ; honorary consul｜名誉領事 ; vice consul｜副領事
tip_ja: consul は領事、consulate は領事館。混同しないこと。
forms: 複数形: consuls

meanings_ja: n. 操作、巧みな操り | n. 取り扱い、操作
definition_en: clever or unfair control of a person or situation for one's own benefit | the skilled handling or adjusting of an object, tool or information
example1_en: She recognised his emotional manipulation and refused to feel guilty.
example1_ja: 彼女は彼の感情的な操作に気づき、罪悪感を抱くことを拒んだ。
example2_en: The manipulation of survey results can mislead policymakers and reduce public trust in scientific research.
example2_ja: 調査結果の操作は、政策立案者を誤らせ、科学的研究への社会の信頼を損なうおそれがある。
collocations: emotional manipulation｜感情の操作 ; data manipulation｜データの加工、データの改ざん ; market manipulation｜市場操作
tip_ja: 人を操る意味では悪い印象。道具や情報の扱いなら中立的。
forms: 複数形: manipulations

meanings_ja: adj. 同時に起こる、並行する
definition_en: happening or existing at the same time
example1_en: Two concurrent meetings meant I had to choose one.
example1_ja: 会議が二つ同時に開かれていたので、どちらかを選ぶしかなかった。
example2_en: Concurrent improvements in housing and public transport can make urban development more inclusive and sustainable.
example2_ja: 住宅と公共交通の同時並行的な改善は、都市開発をより包摂的で持続可能なものにしうる。
collocations: concurrent events｜同時に起こる出来事 ; concurrent sessions｜並行して行われる分科会 ; concurrent with｜〜と同時に
tip_ja: 時間の重なりを強調する語。「〜と同時に」は concurrent with。

meanings_ja: v. お世辞を言う、へつらう | v. うれしがらせる、光栄に思わせる | v. 実物より良く見せる、似合う
definition_en: to praise someone too much, often to please them or gain something | to make someone feel pleased and proud | to make someone or something look more attractive
example1_en: That blue jacket really flatters you in this light.
example1_ja: この光の下だと、その青いジャケットは本当にあなたに似合っている。
example2_en: Advertisements often flatter consumers by suggesting that choosing a particular product demonstrates intelligence or good taste.
example2_ja: 広告は、特定の商品を選べば知性や良い趣味を示せると匂わせて、消費者の気分を持ち上げることが多い。
collocations: flatter someone's ego｜人の自尊心をくすぐる ; feel flattered｜光栄に感じる ; flatter yourself｜うぬぼれる
tip_ja: be flattered は「光栄だ」の意で、必ずしも悪い意味ではない。
forms: 三人称単数現在: flatters | 過去形: flattered | 過去分詞: flattered | 現在分詞: flattering

meanings_ja: v. 干渉する、おせっかいを焼く
definition_en: to get involved in other people's affairs when it is not welcome
example1_en: Please don't meddle in how I arrange my room.
example1_ja: 私の部屋の片づけ方に口を出さないで。
example2_en: Parents who constantly meddle in their children's decisions may prevent them from developing confidence and independence.
example2_ja: 子どもの決定に絶えず干渉する親は、子どもが自信と自立心を育てる妨げになるかもしれない。
collocations: meddle in someone's affairs｜人の事に干渉する ; meddle with something｜物を勝手にいじる
tip_ja: 事柄への干渉は meddle in、物をいじるなら meddle with。
forms: 三人称単数現在: meddles | 過去形: meddled | 過去分詞: meddled | 現在分詞: meddling

meanings_ja: n. 熟考、瞑想 | n. 考慮、予定
definition_en: the act of thinking deeply and quietly about something | the act of thinking about doing something in the future
example1_en: He sat by the lake in quiet contemplation.
example1_ja: 彼は湖のほとりで静かに物思いにふけっていた。
example2_en: Public gardens offer urban residents valuable opportunities for quiet contemplation away from the pressures of daily life.
example2_ja: 公共の庭園は、都市の住民に日常の重圧から離れて静かに思索する貴重な機会を与えてくれる。
collocations: quiet contemplation｜静かな思索 ; deep contemplation｜深い熟考 ; in contemplation｜熟考中で
tip_ja: ふつうは不可算。静かに深く考える意味で、苦悩とは限らない。

meanings_ja: n. 境界、限界点、しきい値 | n. 戸口、入り口 | n. 始まり、出発点
definition_en: the level or point at which something starts to happen or change | the strip of floor at the bottom of a doorway | the beginning of an important new stage or event
example1_en: My brother has a much higher pain threshold than me.
example1_ja: 兄は私よりずっと痛みに強い。
example2_en: Raising the income threshold for financial assistance would allow more low-paid workers to receive support.
example2_ja: 援助を受けられる所得の上限を引き上げれば、低賃金で働くより多くの人が支援を受けられるようになるだろう。
collocations: pain threshold｜痛みの限界点 ; income threshold｜所得の基準額 ; cross the threshold｜戸口をまたぐ ; on the threshold of｜まさに〜の入り口にいて
tip_ja: on the threshold of は「新しい段階の入り口に立つ」という意味で、研究や人生の転機に使える。
forms: 複数形: thresholds

meanings_ja: v. 構成する、占める | v. 〜に相当する、〜になる | v. 設立する、設置する
definition_en: to be the parts that together form something | to be regarded as or amount to something | to officially set up a group or organization
example1_en: Vegetables constitute most of the food in our fridge.
example1_ja: 冷蔵庫の中の食べ物の大半は野菜だ。
example2_en: Rising housing costs constitute a major barrier to financial independence for young adults in large cities.
example2_ja: 住宅費の高騰は、大都市に住む若者が経済的に自立するうえでの大きな障壁となっている。
collocations: constitute a majority｜過半数を占める ; constitute a threat｜脅威となる ; constitute a breach｜違反にあたる ; constitute a committee｜委員会を設立する
tip_ja: 「部分 constitute 全体」の形。be 動詞 + made up of とは主語が逆になる。
forms: 三人称単数現在: constitutes | 過去形: constituted | 過去分詞: constituted | 現在分詞: constituting

meanings_ja: adj. 手術前の
definition_en: happening or done before a surgical operation
example1_en: The nurse explained my preoperative checks before tomorrow's surgery.
example1_ja: 看護師は明日の手術に先立つ術前の検査について説明してくれた。
example2_en: Thorough preoperative assessment helps medical teams identify potential risks and plan appropriate care for each patient.
example2_ja: 手術前の丁寧な評価により、医療チームは潜在的なリスクを見つけ、各患者に適した治療を計画できる。
collocations: preoperative assessment｜術前評価 ; preoperative care｜術前ケア ; preoperative preparation｜術前準備
tip_ja: pre- は「前」。対義語は postoperative（手術後の）。

meanings_ja: adj. 固有の、本来備わっている
definition_en: existing as a natural and permanent part of something
example1_en: Even simple home repairs come with some inherent risks.
example1_ja: 簡単な家の修理にも、ある程度の本質的な危険が伴う。
example2_en: Policymakers must recognise the inherent limitations of economic growth as a measure of social progress and wellbeing.
example2_ja: 政策立案者は、社会の進歩や幸福の尺度としての経済成長が持つ本質的な限界を認識しなければならない。
collocations: inherent risks｜固有のリスク ; inherent limitations｜本質的な限界 ; inherent in｜～に内在する ; inherent value｜内在的価値
tip_ja: inherent in ～の形が多い。後から得たものではなく、もともと備わる性質を表す。

meanings_ja: adj. 実証的な、経験的な
definition_en: based on what is observed or tested, not on theory alone
example1_en: Our garden trial provided empirical evidence that compost helps plants.
example1_ja: 庭での試験で、堆肥が植物の成長を助けるという実証的な証拠が得られた。
example2_en: Education policies should be supported by empirical research rather than assumptions about how children learn.
example2_ja: 教育政策は、子どもの学び方についての思い込みではなく、実証的な研究に裏付けられるべきだ。
collocations: empirical evidence｜実証的証拠 ; empirical research｜実証研究 ; empirical data｜実証データ
tip_ja: 観察や実験に基づくという意味。個人の体験談という意味ではない。

meanings_ja: n. 水辺、ウォーターフロント
definition_en: the part of a town beside a river, lake or sea
example1_en: We walked along the waterfront after an early dinner.
example1_ja: 私たちは早めの夕食のあと、水辺沿いを歩いた。
example2_en: Redeveloping the waterfront can create attractive public spaces, provided that existing residents are not forced to leave.
example2_ja: ウォーターフロントの再開発は魅力的な公共空間を生みうるが、既存の住民が追い出されないことが条件だ。
collocations: along the waterfront｜水辺に沿って ; waterfront development｜ウォーターフロント開発 ; a waterfront restaurant｜水辺のレストラン
tip_ja: 川・湖・海に面した町の一帯を指す。砂浜や海岸とは限らない。
forms: 複数形: waterfronts

meanings_ja: v. 再分配する、配り直す
definition_en: to share something out again in a different way
example1_en: We redistributed the blankets so everyone had one.
example1_ja: 全員に行き渡るよう、毛布を配り直した。
example2_en: Progressive taxation can redistribute wealth and help governments fund essential services for disadvantaged communities.
example2_ja: 累進課税は富を再分配し、政府が恵まれない地域社会のための重要なサービスを支える助けになりうる。
collocations: redistribute wealth｜富を再分配する ; redistribute income｜所得を再分配する ; redistribute resources｜資源を再分配する
tip_ja: 従来の配分を変えるという意味で、必ずしも均等に分けるとは限らない。
forms: 三人称単数現在: redistributes | 過去形: redistributed | 過去分詞: redistributed | 現在分詞: redistributing

meanings_ja: n. 遵守、従うこと、コンプライアンス
definition_en: the act of obeying a rule, law or request
example1_en: The inspector checked our kitchen for compliance with hygiene rules.
example1_ja: 検査官は、衛生規則を守っているか私たちの厨房を点検した。
example2_en: Regular inspections can improve compliance with environmental regulations and reduce pollution from industrial facilities.
example2_ja: 定期的な検査は、環境規制の遵守を高め、工場による汚染を減らしうる。
collocations: compliance with regulations｜規則の遵守 ; ensure compliance｜確実に遵守させる ; in compliance with｜～に従って
tip_ja: 通常は不可算。「～の遵守」は compliance with ～と言う。

meanings_ja: adj. 偽の、うそくさい、いんちきな | n. いかさま師、偽善者
definition_en: not genuine; pretending to be something real or sincere | a person who pretends to be sincere or skilled but is not
example1_en: His phony smile disappeared as soon as we left.
example1_ja: 私たちが去るとすぐ、彼の作り笑いは消えた。
example2_en: Consumers should be cautious about phony online reviews that exaggerate the benefits of health products.
example2_ja: 消費者は、健康食品の効果を誇張する偽のオンラインレビューに注意すべきだ。
collocations: phony smile｜作り笑い ; phony excuse｜見え透いた言い訳 ; phony claims｜虚偽の主張
tip_ja: 口語的な語。英国では phoney と綴ることも多い。
forms: 比較級: phonier | 最上級: phoniest

meanings_ja: adv. 細心の注意を払って、念入りに
definition_en: in a way that shows great care about every small detail
example1_en: She meticulously cleaned each tiny part of the watch.
example1_ja: 彼女は時計の小さな部品を一つ一つ念入りに掃除した。
example2_en: Researchers must meticulously record their procedures so that other teams can reproduce and verify the results.
example2_ja: 研究者は、他のチームが結果を再現し検証できるよう、手順を細部まで丁寧に記録しなければならない。
collocations: meticulously planned｜綿密に計画された ; meticulously documented｜詳細に記録された ; meticulously examine｜入念に調べる
tip_ja: 細部への注意を強調する語。「臆病に」という意味ではない。

meanings_ja: adj. 球形的；球状的
definition_en: shaped like a ball
example1_en: A spherical lamp hung above the dining table.
example1_ja: 餐桌上方挂着一盏球形灯。
example2_en: Researchers use spherical particles of different sizes to investigate how pollutants move through water filtration systems.
example2_ja: 研究人员使用大小不同的球形颗粒，研究污染物如何通过水过滤系统。
collocations: spherical shape｜球形 ; spherical particles｜球形颗粒 ; spherical surface｜球面
tip_ja: spherical指立体球形；circular指平面圆形。

meanings_ja: n. 规格；技术要求
definition_en: A detailed description of how something must be designed or made.
example1_en: Check the specifications before buying a new laptop.
example1_ja: 买新笔记本电脑前，先查看规格参数。
example2_en: Clear building specifications help ensure that new housing meets safety standards and uses energy efficiently.
example2_ja: 明确的建筑技术要求有助于确保新住房符合安全标准并高效利用能源。
collocations: technical specifications｜技术规格 ; meet specifications｜符合规格要求 ; design specification｜设计规范 ; to specification｜按规定规格
tip_ja: 谈产品各项参数常用复数specifications，可简称specs。

meanings_ja: adj. 严重的；强烈的 | adj. 急性的 | adj. 敏锐的
definition_en: Very serious or intense. | Starting suddenly and lasting a short time, often severely. | Quick to notice or understand things.
example1_en: The village faced an acute water shortage last summer.
example1_ja: 去年夏天，这个村庄面临严重缺水。
example2_en: An acute shortage of affordable housing forces many young workers to live far from their workplaces.
example2_ja: 经济适用住房的严重短缺迫使许多年轻劳动者住在远离工作地点的地方。
collocations: acute shortage｜严重短缺 ; acute pain｜剧痛 ; acute illness｜急性疾病 ; acute awareness｜敏锐的意识
tip_ja: 疾病中acute与chronic（慢性的）相对。

meanings_ja: v. 使通风 | v. 公开表达；公开讨论
definition_en: To allow fresh air to enter and circulate through somewhere. | To express or discuss opinions and concerns openly.
example1_en: Open both windows to ventilate the kitchen after cooking.
example1_ja: 做完饭后打开两扇窗，给厨房通风。
example2_en: Schools should ventilate classrooms regularly to improve indoor air quality and create healthier learning environments.
example2_ja: 学校应定期给教室通风，以改善室内空气质量，创造更健康的学习环境。
collocations: ventilate a room｜给房间通风 ; well-ventilated buildings｜通风良好的建筑 ; ventilate grievances｜公开表达不满
tip_ja: 使通风是常用义；表示公开讨论时较正式。

meanings_ja: n. 缩影；微型世界
definition_en: A small system showing the features of a larger one.
example1_en: Our busy kitchen is a microcosm of family life.
example1_ja: 我们忙碌的厨房是家庭生活的一个缩影。
example2_en: A diverse urban neighbourhood can serve as a microcosm of the wider society's opportunities and challenges.
example2_ja: 一个多元化的城市社区可以成为整个社会所面临的机遇与挑战的缩影。
collocations: a microcosm of society｜社会的缩影 ; in microcosm｜以缩影形式 ; serve as a microcosm｜充当缩影
tip_ja: 常用a microcosm of，指缩影，不只是微小事物。

meanings_ja: n. 回顾；回想
definition_en: Consideration of past events, often with a changed understanding.
example1_en: In retrospect, packing extra socks was a brilliant idea.
example1_ja: 现在回想起来，多带几双袜子真是个好主意。
example2_en: In retrospect, investing earlier in public transport could have prevented many of the city's current traffic problems.
example2_ja: 回过头看，如果早点投资公共交通，本可以避免这座城市目前的许多交通问题。
collocations: in retrospect｜回过头看 ; only in retrospect｜只有事后回想才
tip_ja: 通常用于固定短语in retrospect，表示事后回想。

meanings_ja: v. 促进；使便利
definition_en: make an action or process easier
example1_en: These sliding doors facilitate access for people using wheelchairs.
example1_ja: 这些推拉门方便使用轮椅的人进出。
example2_en: Digital platforms can facilitate collaboration between students in different countries, allowing them to exchange ideas more easily.
example2_ja: 数字平台可以促进不同国家学生之间的合作，让他们更容易交流想法。
collocations: facilitate communication｜促进沟通 ; facilitate learning｜促进学习 ; facilitate access｜方便进入或使用
tip_ja: 后接名词或动名词，不用facilitate somebody to do。

meanings_ja: v. 再次发生；反复出现
definition_en: to happen again, especially repeatedly or after an interval
example1_en: If these headaches recur, please speak to your doctor.
example1_ja: 如果这些头痛再次出现，请咨询医生。
example2_en: Traffic congestion will continue to recur unless cities address the underlying causes of excessive car use.
example2_ja: 除非城市解决汽车使用过度的根本原因，否则交通拥堵将继续反复出现。
collocations: a recurring problem｜反复出现的问题 ; a recurring theme｜反复出现的主题 ; symptoms recur｜症状复发
tip_ja: 不及物动词；过去式recurred，分词recurring。

meanings_ja: v. 推翻；颠覆 | n. 推翻；政权覆灭
definition_en: to remove a ruler or government from power | the removal of a ruler or government from power
example1_en: The film follows citizens who overthrow an unfair ruler.
example1_ja: 这部电影讲述民众推翻不公正统治者的故事。
example2_en: Economic hardship can weaken public support for a government and encourage attempts to overthrow it.
example2_ja: 经济困难可能削弱公众对政府的支持，并促使人们尝试推翻它。
collocations: overthrow a government｜推翻政府 ; overthrow a regime｜推翻政权 ; the overthrow of a ruler｜统治者被推翻
tip_ja: 过去式overthrew，过去分词overthrown。

meanings_ja: n. 香；熏香
definition_en: a substance burned to produce a pleasant smell
example1_en: A thin trail of smoke rose from the incense.
example1_ja: 一缕轻烟从熏香上缓缓升起。
example2_en: Burning incense indoors can affect air quality, particularly in small rooms with inadequate ventilation.
example2_ja: 在室内焚香可能影响空气质量，尤其是在通风不足的小房间里。
collocations: burn incense｜焚香 ; incense sticks｜线香 ; incense burner｜香炉
tip_ja: 名词重音在前；同形动词重音在后，意为激怒。

meanings_ja: adj. 异常的；罕见的 | n. 狂热爱好者 | v. 惊慌；吓坏
definition_en: Very unusual and unexpected | Someone extremely interested in a particular activity or subject | To become very frightened or upset, or make someone so
example1_en: A freak hailstorm covered our garden in white ice.
example1_ja: 一场罕见的冰雹把我们的花园盖上了一层白冰。
example2_en: A freak weather event can expose weaknesses in urban infrastructure and disrupt essential public services.
example2_ja: 异常天气事件可能暴露城市基础设施的薄弱环节，并扰乱基本公共服务。
collocations: a freak accident｜离奇的意外事故 ; a freak storm｜罕见的风暴 ; a fitness freak｜健身狂热爱好者 ; freak out｜惊慌失措
tip_ja: 形容词通常置于名词前；动词常用freak out。

meanings_ja: n. 伪造；伪造品
definition_en: Making illegal copies of documents or artworks; such a copy.
example1_en: The painting in the shop was a forgery.
example1_ja: 商店里的那幅画是一件赝品。
example2_en: Museums employ specialists to detect forgery and protect the public from misleading claims about historical objects.
example2_ja: 博物馆聘请专家识别伪造品，避免公众被有关历史文物的不实说法误导。
collocations: document forgery｜文件伪造 ; art forgery｜艺术品伪造 ; detect a forgery｜识别伪造品 ; a convincing forgery｜足以乱真的赝品
tip_ja: forgery是伪造或赝品；锻造作坊是forge。

meanings_ja: n. 容器上缘；口沿 | n. 帽檐 | v. 充满；满溢
definition_en: the upper edge of a cup, bowl, or other container | the part of a hat extending outward around its base | to be full of liquid or a strong feeling
example1_en: She filled my cup to the brim with tea.
example1_ja: 她把我的杯子倒满了茶。
example2_en: Community centres brimming with activity can strengthen social connections and reduce isolation among older residents.
example2_ja: 活动丰富的社区中心能够加强社会联系，减少老年居民的孤独感。
collocations: to the brim｜到满沿；满满地 ; a wide brim｜宽帽檐 ; brim with confidence｜充满信心
tip_ja: 满到杯沿用to the brim；充满用brim with。

meanings_ja: adj. 很可能遭受…的 | adj. 负有法律责任的
definition_en: Likely to experience something, especially something unpleasant. | Legally responsible for something, especially damage or payment.
example1_en: These old pipes are liable to burst in winter.
example1_ja: 这些旧水管在冬天很容易爆裂。
example2_en: Employers may be held liable for injuries caused by unsafe conditions in the workplace.
example2_ja: 雇主可能须对工作场所不安全条件造成的伤害承担法律责任。
collocations: liable to do something｜很可能做某事 ; liable for damages｜负有损害赔偿责任 ; be held liable｜被认定负有法律责任
tip_ja: liable to后接动词表可能；liable for表责任。

meanings_ja: v. 派遣；发送 | n. 发送；派遣 | n. 新闻报道；公文
definition_en: To send someone or something to a particular destination. | The act of sending goods, messages, or people somewhere. | An official message or a report sent by a journalist.
example1_en: The shop dispatched my new shoes this morning.
example1_ja: 商店今天早上寄出了我的新鞋。
example2_en: Local authorities should dispatch emergency teams quickly when severe flooding threatens homes and essential infrastructure.
example2_ja: 当严重洪灾威胁住宅和关键基础设施时，地方政府应迅速派出应急队伍。
collocations: dispatch goods｜发货 ; dispatch a team｜派出队伍 ; ready for dispatch｜备妥待发 ; a news dispatch｜新闻报道
tip_ja: despatch也是正确拼写，但dispatch更常见。

meanings_ja: n. 对齐；排列成直线 | n. 一致；协调 | n. 结盟；政治联合
definition_en: The arrangement of objects in a straight line or correct position. | Agreement between ideas, aims, or actions. | An association between groups sharing political aims or interests.
example1_en: The mechanic checked the alignment of my front wheels.
example1_ja: 修理工检查了我的前轮定位。
example2_en: Closer alignment between school curricula and workplace needs could improve employment prospects for young graduates.
example2_ja: 学校课程与职场需求更加协调，有助于改善年轻毕业生的就业前景。
collocations: wheel alignment｜车轮定位 ; in alignment with｜与……一致 ; political alignment｜政治结盟
tip_ja: in alignment with可指位置对齐或目标一致。

meanings_ja: n. 民主主义者 | n. 美国民主党党员或支持者
definition_en: Someone who supports government based on the people's choices | A member or supporter of the Democratic Party in America
example1_en: As a democrat, she wants everyone to have a vote.
example1_ja: 作为民主主义者，她希望人人都有投票权。
example2_en: A committed democrat should defend fair elections even when the results favour a competing political party.
example2_ja: 坚定的民主主义者即使面对有利于竞争政党的结果，也应捍卫公正的选举。
collocations: committed democrat｜坚定的民主主义者 ; lifelong democrat｜终身信奉民主的人 ; liberal democrat｜自由民主主义者
tip_ja: 泛指民主主义者用小写；美国民主党人写作Democrat。

meanings_ja: n. 恶意；害人之心
definition_en: a desire to hurt someone or cause them trouble
example1_en: There was no malice in his teasing smile.
example1_ja: 他打趣的笑容里并没有恶意。
example2_en: Schools should distinguish between careless remarks and comments made with malice when addressing conflicts among students.
example2_ja: 学校在处理学生之间的冲突时，应区分无心之言和恶意评论。
collocations: with malice｜怀着恶意 ; bear no malice｜不怀恶意 ; out of malice｜出于恶意
tip_ja: 通常不可数；with malice 表示“怀着恶意”。

meanings_ja: n. 认证；资格证明
definition_en: Official confirmation that someone or something meets required standards.
example1_en: The swimming instructor proudly showed us her new certification.
example1_ja: 游泳教练自豪地向我们展示了她新取得的资格证明。
example2_en: Independent certification helps consumers identify products that meet recognised environmental standards throughout the production process.
example2_ja: 独立认证帮助消费者识别在整个生产过程中符合公认环保标准的产品。
collocations: professional certification｜专业资格认证 ; obtain certification｜获得认证 ; certification body｜认证机构 ; certification process｜认证流程
tip_ja: certification重认证；certificate常指证书本身。

meanings_ja: adj. 必需的；必要的 | n. 必需品；必要条件
definition_en: needed for a particular purpose | something necessary for a particular purpose
example1_en: She has the requisite skills to repair this bicycle.
example1_ja: 她具备修理这辆自行车所必需的技能。
example2_en: Applicants without the requisite qualifications may benefit from training programmes designed to improve access to skilled employment.
example2_ja: 不具备必要资历的申请者或可受益于旨在帮助人们进入技术岗位的培训项目。
collocations: requisite skills｜必备技能 ; requisite qualifications｜必要资历 ; a requisite for success｜成功的必要条件
tip_ja: 较正式；requisite 指必需，prerequisite 强调先决。

meanings_ja: n. 欺骗；欺诈
definition_en: Dishonest behaviour intended to make someone believe something false.
example1_en: His deceit became clear when we opened the empty box.
example1_ja: 我们打开空盒子时，他的骗局就暴露了。
example2_en: Deceit in advertising can damage consumer trust and create unfair advantages for companies that misrepresent their products.
example2_ja: 广告中的欺骗行为会损害消费者信任，并让虚假宣传产品的企业获得不公平的优势。
collocations: deliberate deceit｜蓄意欺骗 ; an act of deceit｜欺骗行为 ; lies and deceit｜谎言与欺骗
tip_ja: deceit通常不可数；一次欺骗可用an act of deceit。

meanings_ja: n. 暂停；停职；停学 | n. 车辆悬架 | n. 悬浮液；悬浮状态
definition_en: A temporary stop to an activity or someone's participation | Vehicle parts that reduce shaking on uneven roads | A liquid containing undissolved particles, or their state within it
example1_en: The storm caused the suspension of all ferry services.
example1_ja: 暴风雨导致所有渡轮服务暂停。
example2_en: The temporary suspension of construction work allowed researchers to assess the project's impact on local wildlife.
example2_ja: 建筑工程的暂时停工让研究人员得以评估该项目对当地野生动物的影响。
collocations: suspension of services｜服务暂停 ; school suspension｜停学处分 ; suspension system｜悬架系统 ; in suspension｜处于悬浮状态
tip_ja: 表示暂时中止；车辆语境中指悬架。

meanings_ja: v. 侵占；大量充斥 | v. 超出时间或费用限度 | n. 超时；超支
definition_en: To spread through or occupy a place in unwanted numbers. | To continue beyond an agreed time or cost limit. | An amount by which planned time or costs are exceeded.
example1_en: Weeds have overrun the garden since our neighbours moved away.
example1_ja: 邻居搬走后，花园里就长满了杂草。
example2_en: Major infrastructure projects often overrun their budgets when planners underestimate material costs and construction delays.
example2_ja: 规划者低估材料成本和施工延误时，大型基础设施项目往往会超支。
collocations: be overrun with weeds｜杂草丛生 ; overrun the budget｜超出预算 ; cost overrun｜成本超支
tip_ja: 变化为overran、overrun；名词重音在首音节。

meanings_ja: adj. 起重要作用的 | adj. 器乐的 | n. 器乐曲
definition_en: playing an important part in making something happen | performed with musical instruments rather than voices | a piece of music performed without singing
example1_en: Your advice was instrumental in helping me find work.
example1_ja: 你的建议对我找到工作起了重要作用。
example2_en: Investment in public transport has been instrumental in reducing traffic congestion in several major cities.
example2_ja: 对公共交通的投资在缓解多个大城市的交通拥堵方面起了重要作用。
collocations: be instrumental in｜在……中起重要作用 ; instrumental music｜器乐 ; instrumental version｜器乐版
tip_ja: 表示“起重要作用”时，用 be instrumental in doing。

meanings_ja: n. 剥削；压榨 | n. 开发；利用
definition_en: Unfair treatment of people to gain benefits from their work | Using resources or opportunities to gain an advantage
example1_en: The workers demanded fair wages and protection from exploitation.
example1_ja: 工人们要求合理的工资，并要求得到保护免受剥削。
example2_en: The uncontrolled exploitation of natural resources can damage ecosystems and undermine the livelihoods of communities that depend on them.
example2_ja: 对自然资源的无节制开发会破坏生态系统，并损害依赖这些资源的社区居民的生计。
collocations: labour exploitation｜劳工剥削 ; commercial exploitation｜商业开发 ; exploitation of natural resources｜自然资源的开发利用
tip_ja: 用于人常指剥削；用于资源指开发利用，需看语境。

meanings_ja: n. 镇静药；安定药
definition_en: A drug used to calm people or animals and reduce anxiety.
example1_en: The vet gave the frightened horse a tranquilizer.
example1_ja: 兽医给受惊的马用了一剂镇静药。
example2_en: Doctors should carefully assess the risks before prescribing a tranquilizer to a patient with persistent anxiety.
example2_ja: 医生在给持续焦虑的患者开镇静药之前，应仔细评估风险。
collocations: prescribe a tranquilizer｜开镇静药 ; take a tranquilizer｜服用镇静药 ; tranquilizer dart｜麻醉飞镖
tip_ja: 美式常拼tranquilizer，英式常拼tranquilliser。

meanings_ja: adj. 普遍的；占主导的
definition_en: Most common or influential at a particular time or place.
example1_en: The prevailing mood at dinner was one of relief.
example1_ja: 晚餐时，大家普遍都松了一口气。
example2_en: The prevailing view among urban planners is that reliable public transport can reduce dependence on private cars.
example2_ja: 城市规划者普遍认为，可靠的公共交通能减少人们对私家车的依赖。
collocations: prevailing view｜主流观点 ; prevailing conditions｜当前普遍状况 ; prevailing wind｜盛行风 ; prevailing attitude｜普遍态度
tip_ja: 常置于名词前；prevailing wind指盛行风。

meanings_ja: n. 暂时平静；间歇 | v. 使平静；哄入睡 | v. 使放松警惕
definition_en: A short period when activity or noise becomes less intense. | To calm someone or gently help them fall asleep. | To make someone feel safe when danger may still exist.
example1_en: We stepped outside during a lull in the rain.
example1_ja: 趁雨暂时停歇，我们走到了外面。
example2_en: A temporary lull in economic activity may give businesses time to review their long-term strategies.
example2_ja: 经济活动的暂时放缓可能让企业有时间重新审视其长期战略。
collocations: a lull in activity｜活动的暂时停歇 ; lull someone to sleep｜哄某人入睡 ; lull someone into a false sense of security｜使某人产生虚假的安全感
tip_ja: lull强调暂时平静，不表示彻底结束。

meanings_ja: adj. 极讨厌的；令人反感的
definition_en: extremely unpleasant or offensive
example1_en: An obnoxious passenger played loud music throughout the journey.
example1_ja: 一个讨厌的乘客一路都在大声播放音乐。
example2_en: Obnoxious behaviour on public transport can discourage commuters from using otherwise convenient and affordable services.
example2_ja: 公共交通上的恶劣行为可能让通勤者不愿使用原本便捷又实惠的服务。
collocations: obnoxious behaviour｜令人反感的行为 ; obnoxious remark｜令人厌恶的言论 ; obnoxious person｜讨厌的人
tip_ja: 语气比annoying强，常形容无礼的人或行为。

meanings_ja: v. 下垂；低垂
definition_en: Hang or bend down, often from weakness or tiredness.
example1_en: The flowers began to droop in the afternoon heat.
example1_ja: 鲜花在午后的高温下开始低垂。
example2_en: During prolonged droughts, leaves often droop as plants lose water and struggle to maintain their structure.
example2_ja: 长期干旱期间，植物因失水而难以维持形态，叶片往往会下垂。
collocations: drooping eyelids｜耷拉的眼皮 ; flowers droop｜花朵低垂 ; shoulders droop｜肩膀耷拉下来
tip_ja: 常形容花叶、眼皮或肩膀因缺水、疲倦而下垂。

meanings_ja: n. 匆忙；仓促
definition_en: Speed in acting, often without enough care or thought.
example1_en: In my haste, I left my keys on the table.
example1_ja: 我匆忙之中把钥匙落在了桌上。
example2_en: Policies developed in haste may overlook the needs of vulnerable groups and create additional social problems.
example2_ja: 仓促制定的政策可能忽视弱势群体的需求，并引发更多社会问题。
collocations: in haste｜匆忙地 ; undue haste｜过度仓促 ; make haste｜赶快
tip_ja: 通常为不可数名词；in haste意为匆忙地。

meanings_ja: v. 出汗；流汗
definition_en: to release sweat through your skin, especially when hot
example1_en: I began to perspire while carrying the heavy boxes.
example1_ja: 搬那些沉重的箱子时，我开始出汗了。
example2_en: People perspire more during intense exercise because the body needs to release excess heat.
example2_ja: 剧烈运动时人会出更多汗，因为身体需要散发多余的热量。
collocations: perspire heavily｜大量出汗 ; perspire freely｜汗流不止
tip_ja: 比sweat正式；通常作不及物动词。

meanings_ja: n. 灌溉
definition_en: The supply of water to land so crops can grow.
example1_en: The farm's irrigation system keeps these vegetables growing.
example1_ja: 农场的灌溉系统让这些蔬菜持续生长。
example2_en: Efficient irrigation can increase crop yields while reducing water consumption in regions affected by drought.
example2_ja: 在受干旱影响的地区，高效灌溉可以提高作物产量，同时减少用水量。
collocations: irrigation system｜灌溉系统 ; drip irrigation｜滴灌 ; irrigation canal｜灌溉渠 ; irrigation water｜灌溉用水
tip_ja: 通常为不可数名词；动词形式是irrigate。

meanings_ja: v. 指定；指派 | v. 标明；命名
definition_en: To officially choose someone or something for a particular purpose. | To give something an official name or identifying description.
example1_en: We designated one cupboard for all our cleaning supplies.
example1_ja: 我们指定了一个橱柜专门存放所有清洁用品。
example2_en: Local authorities should designate more urban land as protected green space to improve residents' quality of life.
example2_ja: 地方政府应将更多城市土地划为受保护的绿地，以改善居民的生活质量。
collocations: designate someone as｜指定某人为 ; designate an area for｜划定区域用于 ; designated parking spaces｜指定停车位
tip_ja: designate A as B表示指定或认定A为B。

meanings_ja: v. 减少；减弱；降低 | v. 贬低；轻视
definition_en: to become smaller or weaker, or make something so | to make someone or something seem less important or valuable
example1_en: The pain in my ankle gradually diminished overnight.
example1_ja: 一夜之间，我脚踝的疼痛逐渐减轻了。
example2_en: Investment in reliable public transport can diminish dependence on private cars and improve air quality in crowded cities.
example2_ja: 投资建设可靠的公共交通可以减少对私家车的依赖，改善拥挤城市的空气质量。
collocations: diminish significantly｜显著减少 ; diminish in importance｜重要性降低 ; diminish the impact｜减轻影响 ; diminishing returns｜递减的收益
tip_ja: 既可及物也可不及物：信心可diminish，也可被削弱。

meanings_ja: n. 中间；当中
definition_en: The middle of a place, group, activity, or situation.
example1_en: We found a quiet garden in the midst of town.
example1_ja: 我们在镇中心找到了一座安静的花园。
example2_en: In the midst of rapid urban growth, planners must preserve accessible green spaces for residents.
example2_ja: 在城市快速发展的过程中，规划者必须为居民保留便于到达的绿地。
collocations: in the midst of｜在……之中 ; in our midst｜在我们中间
tip_ja: 通常用于in the midst of，表示身处其中或正值某时。

meanings_ja: n. 宇宙
definition_en: The universe considered as a complete, ordered system.
example1_en: Looking through the telescope made me curious about the cosmos.
example1_ja: 透过望远镜观察让我对宇宙产生了好奇。
example2_en: Studying the cosmos helps scientists investigate how galaxies formed and how the universe has changed over time.
example2_ja: 研究宇宙有助于科学家探究星系如何形成，以及宇宙如何随时间演变。
collocations: explore the cosmos｜探索宇宙 ; the origins of the cosmos｜宇宙的起源 ; the vastness of the cosmos｜宇宙的浩瀚
tip_ja: 表示宇宙时通常用the cosmos。

meanings_ja: v. 潜伏；鬼祟地躲藏 | v. 暗藏；潜在
definition_en: stay hidden, often waiting to do something | exist unnoticed and potentially cause trouble
example1_en: A cat lurked behind the sofa, watching my shoelaces.
example1_ja: 一只猫躲在沙发后面，盯着我的鞋带。
example2_en: Security risks may lurk in outdated software, making regular system updates essential for protecting personal information.
example2_ja: 过时的软件中可能暗藏安全风险，因此定期更新系统对保护个人信息至关重要。
collocations: lurk in the shadows｜潜伏在暗处 ; lurk behind｜潜藏在……背后 ; danger lurks｜危险潜伏
tip_ja: 通常作不及物动词；可用危险等抽象事物作主语。

meanings_ja: v. 执行；强制实施
definition_en: Make sure that people obey a law or rule.
example1_en: The pool staff enforce strict rules about running indoors.
example1_ja: 泳池工作人员严格执行禁止在室内奔跑的规定。
example2_en: Governments must enforce environmental regulations consistently if they want industries to reduce pollution and protect public health.
example2_ja: 政府若希望各行业减少污染、保护公众健康，就必须始终如一地执行环境法规。
collocations: enforce the law｜执法 ; enforce regulations｜执行法规 ; strictly enforce｜严格执行
tip_ja: enforce后接法律或规定；迫使某人做事用force。

meanings_ja: adj. 含蓄的；未明说的 | adj. 内含的；固有的 | adj. 完全的；无疑问的
definition_en: Suggested or understood without being directly stated. | Present as a necessary part of something. | Complete and without doubt, especially describing trust or confidence.
example1_en: Her welcoming smile was an implicit invitation to join.
example1_ja: 她热情的笑容是在默默邀请我们加入。
example2_en: Many workplaces have implicit expectations about overtime, which can make employees reluctant to leave on time.
example2_ja: 许多工作场所对加班有不成文的期待，这可能让员工不敢准时下班。
collocations: implicit agreement｜默契；未明说的协议 ; implicit in｜内含于…… ; implicit trust｜完全的信任 ; implicit assumption｜隐含的假设
tip_ja: implicit指未明说；explicit指清楚明确。

meanings_ja: n. 调解人；调停者
definition_en: Someone who helps opposing sides reach an agreement
example1_en: A mediator helped our neighbours settle their garden fence dispute.
example1_ja: 一位调解人帮助我们的邻居解决了花园围栏纠纷。
example2_en: An independent mediator can help employers and workers negotiate fair conditions without resorting to lengthy legal proceedings.
example2_ja: 独立调解人可以帮助雇主和员工协商公平的工作条件，而不必诉诸漫长的法律程序。
collocations: independent mediator｜独立调解人 ; act as a mediator｜担任调解人 ; appoint a mediator｜任命调解人
tip_ja: 调解人促成双方协议，通常不直接作出裁决。

meanings_ja: n. 中间商；中介人
definition_en: Someone arranging deals or buying goods to sell to others.
example1_en: We bought directly from the farmer, avoiding the middleman.
example1_ja: 我们直接向农民购买，绕过了中间商。
example2_en: Online platforms allow small producers to reach consumers directly, reducing their dependence on a traditional middleman.
example2_ja: 网络平台让小生产者能够直接接触消费者，减少对传统中间商的依赖。
collocations: cut out the middleman｜绕过中间商 ; act as a middleman｜充当中介人
tip_ja: 复数为 middlemen；中性表达可用 intermediary。

meanings_ja: n. 制裁；处罚 | v. 正式批准；许可 | v. 制裁；处罚
definition_en: An official penalty intended to enforce rules or change behaviour. | To officially approve or permit an action. | To impose an official penalty on someone or something.
example1_en: The club imposed a sanction for breaking its rules.
example1_ja: 俱乐部对违反规定的行为作出了处罚。
example2_en: Economic sanctions may influence government policy, but they can also create hardship for ordinary citizens.
example2_ja: 经济制裁可能影响政府政策，但也可能给普通民众带来困苦。
collocations: impose sanctions on｜对……实施制裁 ; lift sanctions｜解除制裁 ; economic sanctions｜经济制裁 ; sanction a proposal｜批准提案
tip_ja: 可指“制裁”或“批准”，含义相反，须看语境。

meanings_ja: n. 匕首；短剑
definition_en: A short pointed knife, usually with two sharp edges.
example1_en: An ancient dagger lay inside the museum's glass case.
example1_ja: 一把古代匕首陈列在博物馆的玻璃展柜里。
example2_en: The discovery of a decorated dagger provides evidence of advanced metalworking skills in this ancient settlement.
example2_ja: 一把带装饰的匕首的发现，证明了这个古代聚居地具备先进的金属加工技艺。
collocations: a ceremonial dagger｜仪式用匕首 ; a sheathed dagger｜入鞘的匕首 ; look daggers at someone｜怒视某人
tip_ja: look daggers at someone是习语，意为怒视某人。

meanings_ja: adj. 水力发电的
definition_en: Relating to electricity produced by the movement of water.
example1_en: We visited a hydroelectric dam during our mountain holiday.
example1_ja: 我们在山区度假时参观了一座水电大坝。
example2_en: Hydroelectric power can reduce dependence on fossil fuels, although large dams may disrupt river ecosystems.
example2_ja: 水力发电可以减少对化石燃料的依赖，但大型水坝可能扰乱河流生态系统。
collocations: hydroelectric power｜水力发电 ; hydroelectric dam｜水电大坝 ; hydroelectric power station｜水力发电站
tip_ja: 常修饰power或power station；名词为hydroelectricity。

meanings_ja: n. 坚持不懈；毅力 | n. 持续存在；存留
definition_en: continued effort despite difficulties or delays | the fact of continuing to exist over time
example1_en: After weeks of practice, his persistence finally paid off.
example1_ja: 经过几周练习，他的坚持终于有了回报。
example2_en: The persistence of poverty suggests that economic growth alone cannot guarantee better living conditions for every household.
example2_ja: 贫困的持续存在表明，仅靠经济增长无法保证每个家庭的生活条件都得到改善。
collocations: show persistence｜表现出毅力 ; persistence pays off｜坚持终有回报 ; the persistence of poverty｜贫困的持续存在
tip_ja: 既可指人的毅力，也可指问题或现象持续存在。

meanings_ja: adv. 通常；在一般情况下
definition_en: Usually, or when conditions are normal.
example1_en: We ordinarily eat outside, but today it is raining.
example1_ja: 我们通常在户外吃饭，但今天下雨了。
example2_en: Public libraries ordinarily provide free internet access, helping residents who cannot afford a connection at home.
example2_ja: 公共图书馆通常提供免费网络，帮助那些无力负担家庭网络费用的居民。
collocations: would ordinarily｜通常会 ; ordinarily available｜通常可获得的 ; ordinarily resident｜通常居住的
tip_ja: 表示“通常”，不表示推测性的“大概”。

meanings_ja: adj. 瞬间发生的；即时的
definition_en: Happening immediately, with no noticeable delay.
example1_en: The relief was almost instantaneous when I removed my shoes.
example1_ja: 我一脱下鞋，几乎立刻就感觉轻松了。
example2_en: Modern communication networks allow almost instantaneous exchanges of information between researchers working on different continents.
example2_ja: 现代通信网络让不同大洲的研究人员几乎能够即时交换信息。
collocations: an instantaneous response｜即时反应 ; instantaneous communication｜即时通信 ; almost instantaneous｜几乎瞬间发生的
tip_ja: 强调几乎没有时间间隔，不等于同时发生。

meanings_ja: n. 日食；月食 | v. 使黯然失色；超越
definition_en: an event when one celestial body blocks another's light | make something seem less important or impressive by comparison
example1_en: We watched the lunar eclipse from our garden last night.
example1_ja: 昨晚我们在花园里观看了月食。
example2_en: Investment in digital services may eclipse spending on traditional infrastructure as economies become increasingly dependent on technology.
example2_ja: 随着经济日益依赖科技，数字服务投资可能超过传统基础设施支出。
collocations: solar eclipse｜日食 ; lunar eclipse｜月食 ; total eclipse｜全食 ; eclipse previous achievements｜使以往成就黯然失色
tip_ja: 日食用solar eclipse，月食用lunar eclipse。

meanings_ja: v. 取回；收回 | v. 开垦；使土地可用 | v. 回收利用
definition_en: Get back something that belongs or previously belonged to you | Make damaged or submerged land suitable for use | Recover useful materials from waste for reuse
example1_en: I returned to the station to reclaim my suitcase.
example1_ja: 我回到车站取回自己的行李箱。
example2_en: Coastal cities sometimes reclaim land from the sea to create space for housing and transport.
example2_ja: 沿海城市有时通过填海造地，为住房和交通设施腾出空间。
collocations: reclaim lost property｜领回失物 ; reclaim land｜开垦土地；填海造地 ; reclaim materials｜回收材料
tip_ja: reclaim强调收回或恢复利用，不只是收集。

meanings_ja: adj. 相关的；切题的
definition_en: directly related to the matter being discussed
example1_en: Lena asked a pertinent question about the repair costs.
example1_ja: 莉娜问了一个关于维修费用的切题问题。
example2_en: Evidence about local air quality is particularly pertinent to discussions of expanding public transport networks.
example2_ja: 有关当地空气质量的证据与扩大公共交通网络的讨论尤其相关。
collocations: pertinent question｜切题的问题 ; pertinent information｜相关信息 ; pertinent to｜与……相关
tip_ja: 常用pertinent to表示与某事相关，语体较正式。

meanings_ja: n. 动物突出的口鼻部
definition_en: the projecting nose and mouth of an animal
example1_en: The pig pushed its snout through the wooden fence.
example1_ja: 那头猪把口鼻部伸过了木栅栏。
example2_en: A pig's sensitive snout helps it locate food beneath the soil, supporting its natural foraging behaviour.
example2_ja: 猪灵敏的口鼻部帮助它找到土壤下的食物，满足其自然觅食的需要。
collocations: a pig's snout｜猪的口鼻部 ; a long snout｜长口鼻部 ; a pointed snout｜尖口鼻部
tip_ja: 不只指猪嘴，也指其他动物突出的口鼻部。

meanings_ja: adj. 轻信的；易受骗的
definition_en: Too willing to believe what others say, even when untrue
example1_en: I was gullible enough to believe his ridiculous story.
example1_ja: 我太轻信了，竟然相信了他那荒唐的故事。
example2_en: Teaching media literacy can help gullible consumers recognise misleading advertisements and make better informed purchasing decisions.
example2_ja: 教授媒介素养可以帮助容易受骗的消费者识别误导性广告，作出更明智的购买决定。
collocations: gullible consumers｜容易受骗的消费者 ; gullible enough to believe｜轻信到竟然相信 ; seem gullible｜显得容易受骗
tip_ja: 带贬义，强调容易相信假话，不等于善良。

meanings_ja: n. 手术刀；解剖刀
definition_en: A small, very sharp knife used in surgery or dissection.
example1_en: The surgeon placed the scalpel on a clean tray.
example1_ja: 外科医生把手术刀放在干净的托盘上。
example2_en: Medical students practise using a scalpel on artificial tissue before developing more advanced surgical skills.
example2_ja: 医学生先在人工组织上练习使用手术刀，再学习更高级的外科技能。
collocations: surgical scalpel｜外科手术刀 ; scalpel blade｜手术刀刀片 ; disposable scalpel｜一次性手术刀
tip_ja: 可数名词，指精细切割用的手术刀或解剖刀。

meanings_ja: n. 布道；讲道 | n. 说教；训诫
definition_en: a religious talk given during a service | a long talk telling someone how they should behave
example1_en: The sermon encouraged everyone to help their neighbours.
example1_ja: 这场布道鼓励大家帮助邻居。
example2_en: A sermon can strengthen community ties by encouraging listeners to support vulnerable people and participate in local projects.
example2_ja: 布道可以鼓励听众帮助弱势群体、参与本地项目，从而加强社区联系。
collocations: deliver a sermon｜进行布道 ; a sermon on kindness｜关于善意的布道 ; preach a sermon｜讲道
tip_ja: 本义为宗教讲道；比喻“说教”时常带不满。

meanings_ja: adv. 借以；通过这种方式
definition_en: By which a particular result is achieved.
example1_en: We have an arrangement whereby we share the cooking.
example1_ja: 我们有个安排，轮流负责做饭。
example2_en: Schools could introduce a system whereby older students provide academic support to younger pupils after lessons.
example2_ja: 学校可以引入一种制度，让高年级学生在课后为低年级学生提供学业帮助。
collocations: a system whereby｜借以实现某事的制度 ; a process whereby｜借以实现某事的过程 ; an arrangement whereby｜据此实行的安排
tip_ja: 正式关系副词，常接在system等词后，相当于by which。

meanings_ja: v. 控制；抑制 | n. 限制；约束 | n. 路缘石（美式）
definition_en: to limit or control something unwanted | a limit on an activity or behaviour | the raised edge between a road and pavement
example1_en: I try to curb my spending by cooking at home.
example1_ja: 我尽量在家做饭，以控制开支。
example2_en: Cities can curb air pollution by improving public transport and encouraging residents to cycle.
example2_ja: 城市可以通过改善公共交通和鼓励居民骑车来抑制空气污染。
collocations: curb spending｜控制开支 ; curb inflation｜抑制通货膨胀 ; a curb on emissions｜对排放的限制
tip_ja: 作动词指抑制；路缘石在英式英语中拼作kerb。

meanings_ja: n. 无穷；无限 | n. 无穷大
definition_en: The state of having no end or limit. | A mathematical concept greater than any finite quantity.
example1_en: The desert seemed to stretch away into infinity.
example1_ja: 沙漠仿佛一直延伸到无穷远处。
example2_en: The concept of infinity allows mathematicians to explore quantities beyond the limits of ordinary measurement.
example2_ja: 无穷的概念使数学家能够研究超出常规测量范围的量。
collocations: stretch into infinity｜延伸至无穷远 ; approach infinity｜趋于无穷大 ; an infinity of possibilities｜无穷的可能性
tip_ja: 不是一般的“大量”；数学中常用趋于无穷大。

meanings_ja: v. 推断；推论
definition_en: to reach a conclusion using evidence rather than direct statements
example1_en: From her muddy shoes, I inferred she had been gardening.
example1_ja: 从她沾满泥土的鞋子，我推断她刚才在做园艺活。
example2_en: Researchers cannot infer that smaller classes improve learning without examining other factors affecting student performance.
example2_ja: 研究人员如果不考察影响学生表现的其他因素，就不能推断小班教学能改善学习效果。
collocations: infer from evidence｜根据证据推断 ; infer that｜推断…… ; reasonably infer｜合理推断
tip_ja: infer是听者推断，imply是说者暗示。

meanings_ja: adj. 兴高采烈的；欣喜若狂的
definition_en: Extremely happy and excited, especially after success or good news.
example1_en: Lina was elated when she finally passed her driving test.
example1_ja: 莉娜终于通过驾照考试时，欣喜万分。
example2_en: Graduates may feel elated after securing their first job, although adjusting to workplace expectations can be challenging.
example2_ja: 毕业生找到第一份工作后可能欣喜万分，尽管适应职场要求并不容易。
collocations: feel elated｜感到欣喜万分 ; elated at the news｜听到消息欣喜万分 ; elated by success｜因成功而欢欣鼓舞
tip_ja: 比happy语气更强，常用于成功或获悉好消息后。

meanings_ja: n. 偿付能力
definition_en: The ability to pay all the debts you owe.
example1_en: The accountant checked the firm's solvency before approving the purchase.
example1_ja: 会计在批准这笔采购前检查了公司的偿付能力。
example2_en: Stricter financial regulation can protect bank solvency and reduce the risk of a wider economic crisis.
example2_ja: 更严格的金融监管能够保障银行的偿付能力，降低更大范围经济危机的风险。
collocations: maintain solvency｜维持偿付能力 ; financial solvency｜财务偿付能力 ; solvency requirements｜偿付能力要求
tip_ja: solvency指偿债能力，不等于盈利能力。

meanings_ja: adj. 高山的；阿尔卑斯山的
definition_en: relating to high mountains, especially the Alps
example1_en: Tiny alpine flowers grew between rocks beside the trail.
example1_ja: 小小的高山花朵生长在小径旁的岩石缝中。
example2_en: Rising temperatures threaten alpine ecosystems by reducing snow cover and forcing mountain species to move higher.
example2_ja: 气温上升使积雪覆盖减少，并迫使山地物种向更高处迁移，从而威胁高山生态系统。
collocations: alpine plants｜高山植物 ; alpine meadows｜高山草甸 ; alpine skiing｜高山滑雪 ; alpine ecosystem｜高山生态系统
tip_ja: 泛指高山环境用小写；专指阿尔卑斯山常大写。

meanings_ja: n. 一批运送的货物 | n. 寄售；委托代销
definition_en: A batch of goods sent to a person or place. | An arrangement where sellers pay suppliers only after goods sell.
example1_en: A consignment of fresh oranges arrived at the shop.
example1_ja: 一批新鲜橙子运到了店里。
example2_en: Delays in inspecting a consignment of medical equipment can disrupt essential services in remote communities.
example2_ja: 一批医疗设备的检验延误，可能会影响偏远社区的基本服务。
collocations: a consignment of goods｜一批货物 ; receive a consignment｜收到一批货物 ; on consignment｜以寄售方式
tip_ja: on consignment指寄售，卖出后再向供货方付款。

meanings_ja: n. 灵长类动物
definition_en: a mammal belonging to the group including humans, monkeys, and apes
example1_en: The guide pointed to a primate swinging between branches.
example1_ja: 导游指着一只在树枝间荡来荡去的灵长类动物。
example2_en: Protecting tropical forests is essential for the survival of many primate species threatened by habitat loss.
example2_ja: 保护热带森林对许多因栖息地丧失而受到威胁的灵长类物种的生存至关重要。
collocations: primate species｜灵长类物种 ; primate behaviour｜灵长类动物的行为 ; non-human primates｜非人灵长类动物
tip_ja: 包括人、猿和猴；并非只指猴子。

meanings_ja: adj. 使人想起的；类似的
definition_en: Reminding you of something because of a similarity.
example1_en: The soup's flavour was reminiscent of my grandmother's cooking.
example1_ja: 这汤的味道让我想起了祖母做的饭菜。
example2_en: The proposed station design is reminiscent of traditional architecture, helping the building blend into its historic surroundings.
example2_ja: 拟建车站的设计令人联想到传统建筑，有助于其融入周围的历史环境。
collocations: reminiscent of childhood｜令人想起童年的 ; strongly reminiscent of｜令人强烈联想到 ; vaguely reminiscent of｜隐约使人想起
tip_ja: 固定搭配be reminiscent of，介词不用about。

meanings_ja: adj. 深远的；强烈的 | adj. 深刻的；深邃的
definition_en: Very great in effect, degree, or intensity. | Showing deep thought, understanding, or insight.
example1_en: Meeting my childhood teacher filled me with profound gratitude.
example1_ja: 见到儿时的老师让我心中充满了深深的感激。
example2_en: Access to reliable internet has had a profound impact on educational opportunities in remote communities.
example2_ja: 可靠的互联网接入对偏远社区的教育机会产生了深远影响。
collocations: a profound impact｜深远的影响 ; profound changes｜深刻的变化 ; profound understanding｜深刻的理解 ; profound sadness｜深切的悲伤
tip_ja: 常修饰impact、change、understanding，不指物理深度。

meanings_ja: adj. 违法的；有不良行为的 | adj. 逾期未付的；拖欠的 | n. 违法者；少年犯
definition_en: Behaving illegally or antisocially, especially while young. | Not paid on time, or failing to pay on time. | A person, usually young, who breaks the law.
example1_en: The youth centre helps teenagers change their delinquent behaviour.
example1_ja: 这家青少年中心帮助青少年改正违法行为。
example2_en: Early support for vulnerable families may reduce delinquent behaviour more effectively than harsher punishments alone.
example2_ja: 及早扶助弱势家庭，可能比单纯加重惩罚更有效地减少违法行为。
collocations: delinquent behaviour｜违法行为 ; a juvenile delinquent｜少年犯 ; delinquent payments｜逾期款项 ; a delinquent borrower｜拖欠还款的借款人
tip_ja: 金融语境中指逾期未付；日常多指青少年违法。

meanings_ja: v. 大步走 | n. 大步；步幅 | n. 显著进展
definition_en: Walk with long, confident steps. | A long step taken while walking or running. | Important progress towards a goal, usually expressed in the plural.
example1_en: Leila strode across the platform to catch her train.
example1_ja: 莱拉大步穿过站台去赶火车。
example2_en: Many countries have made significant strides in improving access to primary education over recent decades.
example2_ja: 近几十年来，许多国家在扩大初等教育机会方面取得了显著进展。
collocations: stride across a room｜大步穿过房间 ; make great strides｜取得巨大进展 ; take something in your stride｜从容应对某事
tip_ja: 过去式strode，过去分词stridden；进展常用strides。

meanings_ja: n. 独家权；专有性 | n. 排他性；仅限少数人享有
definition_en: the right to provide or use something without competitors | the quality of being available only to a select group
example1_en: The bakery secured exclusivity to sell bread at the festival.
example1_ja: 这家面包店取得了在该节庆活动中独家销售面包的权利。
example2_en: Although exclusivity agreements can encourage investment, they may also limit competition and raise prices for consumers.
example2_ja: 虽然独家协议能够鼓励投资，但也可能限制竞争并推高消费者支付的价格。
collocations: an exclusivity agreement｜独家协议 ; grant exclusivity｜授予独家权 ; a sense of exclusivity｜专属感
tip_ja: 既可指商业独家权，也可指仅少数人享有的特性。

meanings_ja: n. 动物学
definition_en: the scientific study of animals
example1_en: My cousin studies zoology and spends weekends watching birds.
example1_ja: 我的表亲学习动物学，周末常去观察鸟类。
example2_en: Research in zoology helps scientists understand animal behaviour and design more effective strategies for protecting endangered species.
example2_ja: 动物学研究帮助科学家理解动物行为，并制定更有效的濒危物种保护策略。
collocations: study zoology｜学习动物学 ; a degree in zoology｜动物学学位 ; a zoology department｜动物学系
tip_ja: 通常为不可数名词；研究植物的学科是botany。

meanings_ja: n. 变体；变种 | adj. 变异的；不同的
definition_en: A form that differs slightly from other related forms. | Differing in some way from the usual or related form.
example1_en: This local variant of the soup includes fresh beans.
example1_ja: 这种汤的本地做法加入了新鲜豆子。
example2_en: A genetic variant may affect how individuals respond to certain medicines, making personalised treatment increasingly important.
example2_ja: 某种基因变异可能影响个体对特定药物的反应，因此个性化治疗日益重要。
collocations: a variant of｜……的一种变体 ; genetic variant｜基因变异 ; regional variant｜地区变体 ; variant spelling｜异体拼写
tip_ja: 名词常用a variant of；形容词可修饰spelling等。

meanings_ja: n. 公社；共同生活群体
definition_en: a group living together and sharing possessions and responsibilities
example1_en: They live in a commune and grow vegetables together.
example1_ja: 他们住在一个共同生活的群体中，一起种菜。
example2_en: Living in a commune can reduce individual expenses, but shared decision-making requires patience and effective communication.
example2_ja: 公社生活可以减少个人开支，但共同决策需要耐心和有效沟通。
collocations: live in a commune｜在公社生活 ; farming commune｜农业公社 ; establish a commune｜建立公社
tip_ja: 名词指共同生活群体；动词 commune with 指心灵交流。

meanings_ja: v. 十分恼怒；生闷气 | n. 有害或刺鼻的烟气
definition_en: To feel or express strong anger. | Strong, unpleasant or harmful gas or smoke, usually plural.
example1_en: He fumed when muddy shoes stained his clean carpet.
example1_ja: 泥鞋弄脏了他干净的地毯，他气坏了。
example2_en: Exposure to exhaust fumes can worsen respiratory conditions, particularly among children living near busy roads.
example2_ja: 接触汽车尾气可能加重呼吸系统疾病，尤其会影响住在繁忙道路附近的儿童。
collocations: fume over something｜为某事大发脾气 ; exhaust fumes｜汽车尾气 ; toxic fumes｜有毒烟气
tip_ja: 表示烟气通常用复数fumes；动词常指十分恼怒。

meanings_ja: adv. 从今以后
definition_en: from this time onwards
example1_en: Henceforth, we will keep spare keys in this drawer.
example1_ja: 从今以后，我们会把备用钥匙放在这个抽屉里。
example2_en: The university announced that all new buildings would henceforth meet stricter environmental standards.
example2_ja: 大学宣布，今后所有新建建筑都将达到更严格的环保标准。
collocations: shall henceforth｜今后将 ; be henceforth known as｜从此被称为
tip_ja: 正式用语；日常交流多用 from now on。

meanings_ja: adj. 装满的；负载的 | adj. 充满某种情绪的
definition_en: Carrying or holding a large amount of something. | Full of a particular feeling, especially an unpleasant one.
example1_en: She arrived at the picnic laden with bags of food.
example1_ja: 她带着大包小包的食物来到野餐地点。
example2_en: Trucks laden with construction materials contribute to congestion and increase road maintenance costs in rapidly expanding cities.
example2_ja: 在迅速扩张的城市中，满载建筑材料的卡车加剧了拥堵，并增加了道路维护成本。
collocations: laden with｜装满；充满 ; heavily laden｜满载的 ; a laden truck｜满载的卡车
tip_ja: 常用laden with；也可构成sugar-laden等复合形容词。

meanings_ja: adj. 最大的；极度的 | n. 最大努力；极限
definition_en: greatest in degree, amount, or intensity | the greatest effort or amount someone can achieve
example1_en: Please handle this delicate glass bowl with utmost care.
example1_ja: 请极其小心地拿放这只易碎的玻璃碗。
example2_en: Protecting patient privacy is of the utmost importance when hospitals introduce digital systems for storing medical records.
example2_ja: 医院引入电子病历存储系统时，保护患者隐私至关重要。
collocations: of the utmost importance｜极为重要 ; with utmost care｜极其小心地 ; do your utmost｜尽最大努力 ; utmost respect｜最高敬意
tip_ja: do one's utmost意为尽最大努力，常接to do。

meanings_ja: adj. 辅助的；备用的 | n. 助动词
definition_en: providing extra help or support when needed | a verb used with another verb to form grammatical structures
example1_en: The boat has an auxiliary engine for emergencies.
example1_ja: 这艘船装有一台应急用的备用发动机。
example2_en: Hospitals require auxiliary power systems to maintain essential medical services during unexpected electricity failures.
example2_ja: 医院需要备用供电系统，以便在意外停电时维持必要的医疗服务。

example1_ja: 他们的小住宅俯瞰着一段宁静的河流。
example2_en: Every new dwelling should meet energy efficiency standards to reduce household costs and environmental damage.
example2_ja: 每一处新建住宅都应达到能效标准，以降低家庭开支并减少环境损害。
collocations: private dwelling｜私人住宅 ; permanent dwelling｜永久住所 ; dwelling place｜居住地
tip_ja: 可数名词，较正式；日常谈论自己的家通常用home。

meanings_ja: n. 星号
definition_en: A star-shaped symbol used to indicate a note or omission
example1_en: An asterisk beside the price points to extra delivery charges.
example1_ja: 价格旁的星号提示还有额外运费。
example2_en: Researchers often use an asterisk in tables to indicate results that meet a particular statistical threshold.
example2_ja: 研究人员常在表格中用星号标明达到特定统计阈值的结果。
collocations: mark with an asterisk｜用星号标记 ; an asterisk beside｜旁边的星号 ; add an asterisk｜添加星号
tip_ja: 词尾是-risk，注意不要误读成-riks。

meanings_ja: v. 合并；融合
definition_en: Combine or join together to form a single whole.
example1_en: The two narrow paths merge just beyond the bridge.
example1_ja: 这两条小路在桥的那一头汇合。
example2_en: Small businesses may merge to reduce operating costs and compete more effectively with larger companies.
example2_ja: 小企业可能通过合并降低运营成本，从而更有效地与大公司竞争。
collocations: merge with another company｜与另一家公司合并 ; merge into one｜合为一体 ; merge two departments｜合并两个部门
tip_ja: merge with表示与……合并；merge into表示并入。

meanings_ja: n. 恶名；声名狼藉
definition_en: the state of being widely known for something bad
example1_en: The restaurant gained notoriety for its dirty kitchen.
example1_ja: 这家餐馆因厨房脏乱而臭名远扬。
example2_en: Some companies gain notoriety for environmental damage, making it harder for them to attract skilled workers.
example2_ja: 一些企业因破坏环境而声名狼藉，因而更难吸引技术人才。
collocations: gain notoriety｜落得恶名 ; notoriety for corruption｜腐败的恶名 ; achieve notoriety｜变得臭名昭著
tip_ja: 通常不可数，含贬义；中性的“名气”用fame。

meanings_ja: n. 微光；闪烁的弱光 | n. 一丝；微弱迹象 | v. 发出微光；隐约闪烁
definition_en: A faint light, often shining unevenly | A small sign of something, especially hope or understanding | To shine faintly or with an unsteady light
example1_en: A glimmer of candlelight escaped through the closed curtains.
example1_ja: 一缕烛光从拉拢的窗帘缝隙中透出来。
example2_en: Recent improvements in water quality offer a glimmer of hope for communities affected by industrial pollution.
example2_ja: 近期水质的改善为受工业污染影响的社区带来了一线希望。
collocations: a glimmer of light｜一缕微光 ; a glimmer of hope｜一线希望 ; a glimmer of understanding｜一丝领悟
tip_ja: a glimmer of hope是“一线希望”的常见表达。

meanings_ja: n. 官僚体制；行政体系 | n. 繁文缛节；官僚作风
definition_en: an administrative system run by officials following established rules | complicated official procedures that make tasks unnecessarily difficult
example1_en: My aunt works within the city's large bureaucracy.
example1_ja: 我姑姑在这个城市庞大的行政体系内工作。
example2_en: Reducing unnecessary bureaucracy could help small businesses obtain permits more quickly without weakening essential safety standards.
example2_ja: 减少不必要的繁文缛节，能帮助小企业更快取得许可证，同时不削弱必要的安全标准。
collocations: government bureaucracy｜政府行政体系 ; reduce bureaucracy｜减少繁文缛节 ; excessive bureaucracy｜过度繁琐的行政手续
tip_ja: bureaucracy指体制或繁琐手续；官僚个人是bureaucrat。

meanings_ja: v. 使协调；使一致 | v. 使和解 | v. 使接受不愉快的现实
definition_en: To make conflicting ideas, needs, or facts compatible | To restore friendly relations after a disagreement | To help someone accept an unpleasant situation
example1_en: We reconciled our different tastes by choosing a buffet.
example1_ja: 我们选择了自助餐，兼顾了彼此不同的口味。
example2_en: Governments must reconcile the demand for affordable housing with the need to protect valuable green spaces.
example2_ja: 政府必须协调可负担住房需求与保护宝贵绿地的需要。
collocations: reconcile A with B｜使A与B协调 ; reconcile differences｜调和分歧 ; be reconciled with someone｜与某人和解 ; reconcile yourself to｜使自己接受
tip_ja: 协调两者用with；接受现实用reconcile oneself to。

meanings_ja: n. 血浆 | n. 等离子体
definition_en: The liquid part of blood in which blood cells float | An ionised gas containing free electrons and charged particles
example1_en: My cousin donates plasma at the local clinic.
example1_ja: 我的表亲在当地诊所捐献血浆。
example2_en: Donated plasma contains proteins that can be used to produce treatments for certain immune system disorders.
example2_ja: 捐献的血浆含有可用于生产某些免疫系统疾病治疗药物的蛋白质。
collocations: blood plasma｜血浆 ; donate plasma｜捐献血浆 ; plasma proteins｜血浆蛋白 ; plasma physics｜等离子体物理学
tip_ja: 通常不可数；医学中指血浆，物理学中指等离子体。

meanings_ja: adj. 不必要的；多余的
definition_en: not necessary and therefore best avoided
example1_en: Calling ahead saved us a needless trip across town.
example1_ja: 提前打个电话，让我们免于白跑一趟穿过全城。
example2_en: Clear guidance on public services can prevent needless confusion and help residents access essential support.
example2_ja: 清晰的公共服务指南可以避免不必要的困惑，帮助居民获得必要的支持。
collocations: needless worry｜不必要的担忧 ; needless expense｜不必要的开支 ; needless to say｜不用说
tip_ja: needless to say意为“不用说”，常作插入语。

meanings_ja: v. 猛涨；飞速上升
definition_en: To increase extremely quickly to a very high level.
example1_en: Our heating bills skyrocketed during the unusually cold winter.
example1_ja: 那个异常寒冷的冬天，我们的取暖费猛涨。
example2_en: Housing costs can skyrocket when population growth outpaces construction, making affordable accommodation increasingly difficult to find.
example2_ja: 当人口增长超过住房建设速度时，住房成本可能猛涨，让人越来越难找到负担得起的住所。
collocations: prices skyrocket｜价格猛涨 ; demand skyrockets｜需求激增 ; skyrocketing costs｜飞涨的成本
tip_ja: 通常作不及物动词，主语常为价格、成本或需求。

meanings_ja: adj. 大气的；大气层的 | adj. 富有氛围的
definition_en: Relating to the gases surrounding Earth or another planet. | Creating a strong and distinctive mood or feeling.
example1_en: We found an atmospheric café tucked behind the old theatre.
example1_ja: 我们在老剧院后面发现了一家很有氛围的咖啡馆。
example2_en: Changes in atmospheric conditions can affect agricultural production and increase the frequency of extreme weather events.
example2_ja: 大气状况的变化会影响农业生产，并增加极端天气事件发生的频率。
collocations: atmospheric pressure｜大气压 ; atmospheric conditions｜大气状况 ; atmospheric pollution｜大气污染 ; an atmospheric setting｜富有氛围的环境
tip_ja: 修饰pressure指大气的；修饰场所常指富有氛围的。

meanings_ja: n. 建立；设立 | n. 机构；营业场所 | n. 权势集团；当权派
definition_en: the process of starting an organisation or system | an organisation or place where business or public activities happen | the powerful people who control a society or profession
example1_en: The establishment of our local club brought neighbours together.
example1_ja: 我们本地俱乐部的成立让邻居们走到了一起。
example2_en: The establishment of protected marine areas can help restore fish populations and support coastal communities.
example2_ja: 设立海洋保护区有助于恢复鱼类种群，并为沿海社区提供支持。
collocations: the establishment of｜……的建立 ; educational establishment｜教育机构 ; business establishment｜营业机构 ; the political establishment｜政治权势集团
tip_ja: 表示建立时不可数；表示机构时可数。

meanings_ja: n. 内部通知；备忘录 | n. 正式备忘录
definition_en: A written message sharing information within an organisation | A formal document recording an agreement or shared intentions
example1_en: The manager sent a memorandum about our new working hours.
example1_ja: 经理发了一份关于新工作时间的内部通知。
example2_en: The two universities signed a memorandum of understanding to support joint research into renewable energy.
example2_ja: 两所大学签署了谅解备忘录，以支持可再生能源领域的联合研究。
collocations: an internal memorandum｜内部备忘录 ; issue a memorandum｜发布备忘录 ; memorandum of understanding｜谅解备忘录
tip_ja: 常简称memo；复数为memoranda或memorandums。

meanings_ja: adj. 合同规定的；契约的
definition_en: Relating to or required by a legal agreement.
example1_en: Fixing the heating is the landlord's contractual responsibility.
example1_ja: 修好暖气是房东按合同应承担的责任。
example2_en: Employers should explain contractual obligations clearly so that workers understand their rights before accepting a position.
example2_ja: 雇主应清楚说明合同义务，让劳动者在接受职位前了解自己的权利。
collocations: contractual obligations｜合同义务 ; contractual rights｜合同权利 ; contractual terms｜合同条款 ; contractual agreement｜契约协议
tip_ja: 强调合同规定的权利或义务，常置于名词前。

meanings_ja: v. 表扬；称赞 | v. 推荐
definition_en: to praise someone or something, often publicly | to recommend someone or something as worthy of consideration
example1_en: The coach commended Lina for helping her teammates.
example1_ja: 教练表扬莉娜帮助了队友。
example2_en: Inspectors commended the school for providing additional support to students with different learning needs.
example2_ja: 督察人员赞扬该校为有不同学习需求的学生提供额外支持。
collocations: commend someone for something｜因某事表扬某人 ; highly commended｜受到高度赞扬 ; commend something to someone｜向某人推荐某物
tip_ja: commend是称赞；command是命令，注意拼写。

meanings_ja: n. 冷漠；不关心
definition_en: A lack of interest, concern, or emotional response.
example1_en: Her indifference surprised me when I shared my exciting news.
example1_ja: 我分享令人兴奋的消息时，她的冷淡让我很意外。
example2_en: Public indifference to local elections can weaken accountability and reduce the quality of democratic representation.
example2_ja: 公众对地方选举漠不关心，可能削弱问责机制并降低民主代表的质量。
collocations: indifference to suffering｜对苦难的漠视 ; public indifference｜公众的冷漠 ; show indifference｜表现冷淡
tip_ja: 通常不可数；对某事冷漠用 indifference to。

meanings_ja: v. 与……矛盾；相抵触 | v. 反驳；否认某人的话
definition_en: To be inconsistent with another statement, fact, or piece of evidence. | To say that someone else's statement is wrong.
example1_en: Your muddy shoes contradict your claim about staying indoors.
example1_ja: 你说自己一直待在室内，但你鞋上的泥可不是这么回事。
example2_en: Recent findings contradict the assumption that longer working hours necessarily lead to higher levels of productivity.
example2_ja: 近期研究结果与“工作时间越长，生产效率必然越高”的假设相矛盾。
collocations: contradict a claim｜与某一说法矛盾 ; contradict the evidence｜与证据相悖 ; contradict yourself｜自相矛盾
tip_ja: 及物动词，直接接人或说法；无需加with。

meanings_ja: v. 讲述；叙述 | v. 为…作旁白
definition_en: To tell a story or describe a series of events. | To provide spoken commentary for a film or programme.
example1_en: My grandfather loves to narrate stories from his childhood.
example1_ja: 我祖父很喜欢讲述他童年的故事。
example2_en: Local residents narrate their experiences in the documentary, offering valuable insights into urban change.
example2_ja: 当地居民在纪录片中讲述亲身经历，为理解城市变迁提供了宝贵视角。
collocations: narrate a story｜讲述故事 ; narrate a documentary｜为纪录片配旁白 ; narrate events｜叙述事件
tip_ja: 及物动词，直接接故事或事件，无需加about。

meanings_ja: n. 玻璃器皿
definition_en: objects made of glass, especially drinking vessels or laboratory equipment
example1_en: Please wrap the glassware carefully before packing the box.
example1_ja: 装箱前请把玻璃器皿仔细包好。
example2_en: Reusable glassware can reduce waste in laboratories, provided that appropriate cleaning and safety procedures are followed.
example2_ja: 只要遵循适当的清洁和安全程序，可重复使用的玻璃器皿就能减少实验室废弃物。
collocations: laboratory glassware｜实验室玻璃器皿 ; delicate glassware｜易碎的玻璃器皿 ; wash glassware｜清洗玻璃器皿
tip_ja: 不可数名词；一件玻璃器皿用a piece of glassware。

meanings_ja: adj. 省的；省级的 | adj. 外省的；地方的 | adj. 狭隘守旧的
definition_en: relating to a province or its administration | relating to areas outside a country's capital | showing limited experience and unwillingness to accept different ideas
example1_en: She works at the provincial hospital near our home.
example1_ja: 她在我们家附近的省立医院工作。
example2_en: Provincial governments can adapt national education policies to meet the specific needs of local communities.
example2_ja: 省级政府可以调整国家教育政策，以满足当地社区的具体需求。
collocations: provincial government｜省级政府 ; provincial capital｜省会 ; provincial town｜外省城镇
tip_ja: 指省级时中性；形容人的观念时可含贬义。

meanings_ja: v. 设想；展望
definition_en: To imagine a possible future situation or event.
example1_en: I envisage turning this spare room into a studio.
example1_ja: 我设想把这间空房改成工作室。
example2_en: Urban planners envisage a future in which most residents can reach essential services on foot.
example2_ja: 城市规划者设想，未来大多数居民都能步行到达提供基本服务的场所。
collocations: envisage a future｜展望未来 ; envisage doing something｜设想做某事 ; as originally envisaged｜按最初的设想
tip_ja: 后接名词、动名词或that从句，不接to do。

meanings_ja: n. 尊重；敬重 | v. 尊重；敬重
definition_en: Respect and admiration for someone. | To respect and admire someone highly.
example1_en: Her neighbours hold her in esteem for her kindness.
example1_ja: 邻居们因她的善良而敬重她。
example2_en: Teachers who treat students fairly often earn the lasting esteem of their local communities.
example2_ja: 公平对待学生的教师往往能赢得当地社区长久的敬重。
collocations: hold someone in high esteem｜非常敬重某人 ; earn someone's esteem｜赢得某人的敬重 ; mutual esteem｜相互尊重
tip_ja: 常用hold someone in high esteem表示非常敬重某人。

meanings_ja: adj. 司法的；法院的
definition_en: relating to courts, judges, or the administration of justice
example1_en: The lawyer explained the judicial process to our family.
example1_ja: 律师向我们一家解释了司法程序。
example2_en: An independent judicial system helps protect individual rights and ensures that governments remain accountable.
example2_ja: 独立的司法体系有助于保护个人权利，并确保政府承担责任。
collocations: judicial system｜司法体系 ; judicial review｜司法审查 ; judicial independence｜司法独立
tip_ja: judicial指司法；judicious指明智、审慎。

meanings_ja: v. 限制；使局限于 | v. 禁闭；使无法离开
definition_en: To keep something within particular limits | To keep someone in a place they cannot leave
example1_en: Please confine your muddy boots to the porch.
example1_ja: 请把沾满泥的靴子放在门廊里，别带进屋。
example2_en: Researchers should not confine their investigation to wealthy neighbourhoods when studying access to public transport.
example2_ja: 研究公共交通的可及性时，研究人员不应将调查局限于富裕社区。
collocations: confine something to｜将某事物限制在 ; be confined to bed｜卧床不起 ; confine oneself to｜使自己局限于
tip_ja: 常用confine A to B，表示将A限制在B内。

meanings_ja: n. 半导体
definition_en: A material that conducts electricity less easily than most metals.
example1_en: My sister works at a factory making semiconductor chips.
example1_ja: 我姐姐在一家生产半导体芯片的工厂工作。
example2_en: Investment in semiconductor manufacturing is essential for developing reliable supplies of components used in modern electronic devices.
example2_ja: 投资半导体制造业对于确保现代电子设备所用元件的可靠供应至关重要。
collocations: semiconductor chips｜半导体芯片 ; semiconductor manufacturing｜半导体制造 ; the semiconductor industry｜半导体产业
tip_ja: semi-表示半；半导体导电性介于导体与绝缘体之间。

meanings_ja: n. 缺乏；不足 | n. 缺陷；不足之处
definition_en: A lack of enough of something necessary. | A weakness that prevents something from working well.
example1_en: A blood test revealed that I had an iron deficiency.
example1_ja: 验血结果显示我缺铁。
example2_en: Nutritional deficiency among children can affect physical growth and reduce their ability to concentrate at school.
example2_ja: 儿童营养不足可能影响身体发育，并降低他们在学校集中注意力的能力。
collocations: iron deficiency｜缺铁 ; vitamin deficiency｜维生素缺乏 ; nutritional deficiency｜营养不足 ; remedy a deficiency｜弥补不足
tip_ja: 缺某物用deficiency in；具体缺陷常用复数。

meanings_ja: v. 烧焦；烤焦；使枯萎
definition_en: To burn a surface slightly or damage it with heat
example1_en: The hot iron scorched my favourite cotton shirt.
example1_ja: 滚烫的熨斗把我最喜欢的棉衬衫烫焦了。
example2_en: Prolonged heatwaves can scorch crops, reducing agricultural yields and threatening food supplies in vulnerable regions.
example2_ja: 持续的热浪会使庄稼焦枯，降低农业产量，并威胁脆弱地区的粮食供应。
collocations: scorch marks｜焦痕 ; scorch the grass｜使草地焦枯 ; scorching heat｜灼热
tip_ja: 常指表面烧焦，不一定烧毁；太阳也能scorch植物。

meanings_ja: n. 对称；对称性
definition_en: The matching arrangement of parts on opposite sides.
example1_en: The butterfly's open wings show beautiful symmetry in the sunlight.
example1_ja: 阳光下，蝴蝶展开的双翅呈现出优美的对称性。
example2_en: Architects often use symmetry to create buildings that appear balanced and visually pleasing to visitors.
example2_ja: 建筑师常利用对称性，使建筑在参观者眼中显得平衡而美观。
collocations: perfect symmetry｜完美对称 ; bilateral symmetry｜左右对称 ; radial symmetry｜辐射对称
tip_ja: 通常为不可数名词；形容词是symmetrical。

meanings_ja: n. 不识字；文盲状态 | n. 某领域的知识匮乏
definition_en: The inability to read and write. | A lack of basic knowledge in a particular subject.
example1_en: Evening classes helped my grandfather overcome illiteracy and read independently.
example1_ja: 夜校课程帮助我祖父摆脱了文盲状态，能够独立阅读。
example2_en: Reducing adult illiteracy can improve employment opportunities and enable more people to participate fully in society.
example2_ja: 降低成人文盲率可以改善就业机会，让更多人充分参与社会生活。
collocations: adult illiteracy｜成人文盲现象 ; illiteracy rate｜文盲率 ; combat illiteracy｜扫除文盲 ; financial illiteracy｜金融知识匮乏
tip_ja: illiteracy指不识字的状态；指人宜用描述性表达。

meanings_ja: n. 灾难；重大不幸
definition_en: An event causing severe damage, suffering, or distress.
example1_en: The flood was a calamity for the whole village.
example1_ja: 这场洪水给整个村庄带来了灾难。
example2_en: Effective emergency planning can reduce the human and economic costs of a natural calamity.
example2_ja: 有效的应急规划可以减少自然灾难造成的人员损失和经济代价。
collocations: a natural calamity｜自然灾难 ; avert a calamity｜避免灾难 ; calamity strikes｜灾难降临
tip_ja: 比problem严重得多，常指造成重大损失的灾难。

meanings_ja: n. 外交；外交活动 | n. 交际手腕；圆通
definition_en: Managing relations between countries through discussion and negotiation. | Skill in dealing with people without upsetting them.
example1_en: The two countries solved their disagreement through diplomacy.
example1_ja: 这两个国家通过外交途径解决了分歧。
example2_en: Effective diplomacy can help neighbouring countries manage shared water resources without resorting to conflict.
example2_ja: 有效的外交能帮助邻国管理共享水资源，避免诉诸冲突。
collocations: international diplomacy｜国际外交 ; quiet diplomacy｜低调外交 ; use diplomacy｜运用交际手腕
tip_ja: 既指国家间的外交，也指避免得罪人的处事技巧。

meanings_ja: n. 运输；运送 | n. 公共交通系统
definition_en: the movement of people or goods between places | a system of buses, trains, or other shared transport
example1_en: The glasses broke while they were in transit.
example1_ja: 这些玻璃杯在运输途中破碎了。
example2_en: Investment in public transit can reduce traffic congestion and improve access to employment in growing cities.
example2_ja: 投资公共交通可以缓解交通拥堵，并改善发展中城市居民的就业可达性。
collocations: in transit｜在运输途中 ; public transit｜公共交通 ; transit system｜公共交通系统 ; transit visa｜过境签证
tip_ja: in transit指运输途中；public transit多用于美式英语。

meanings_ja: adj. 耐……的；有抵抗力的 | adj. 抵触的；抗拒的
