meanings_ja: adj. 协同一致的；共同筹划的 | adj. 全力以赴的
definition_en: Planned and carried out together to achieve a shared goal. | Involving determined effort directed towards a particular goal.
example1_en: Our concerted efforts finally cleared the garden of rubbish.
example1_ja: 我们齐心协力，终于清除了花园里的垃圾。
example2_en: Reducing urban air pollution requires concerted action from local authorities, transport providers, businesses and residents.
example2_ja: 减少城市空气污染需要地方政府、交通服务商、企业和居民采取协同行动。
collocations: concerted effort｜共同努力；全力投入 ; concerted action｜协同行动 ; concerted campaign｜联合开展的运动
tip_ja: 常修饰effort或action，强调协同或集中全力。

meanings_ja: n. 北美大草原
definition_en: A broad, mostly treeless grassland in North America
example1_en: We watched tall grass ripple across the open prairie.
example1_ja: 我们看着高高的草在开阔的大草原上起伏。
example2_en: Protecting native prairie habitats helps preserve biodiversity and maintains grassland ecosystems that store substantial amounts of carbon.
example2_ja: 保护原生北美草原生境有助于维护生物多样性，并维持储存大量碳的草原生态系统。
collocations: prairie grass｜草原牧草 ; native prairie｜原生北美草原 ; prairie conservation｜北美草原保护
tip_ja: 通常特指北美草原；泛指草地可用 grassland。

meanings_ja: adj. 强大的；巨大的 | adv. 非常；很
definition_en: Very strong, powerful, or large. | Very; used informally to make a description stronger.
example1_en: A mighty oak stood in the middle of the field.
example1_ja: 田野中央矗立着一棵高大的橡树。
example2_en: Although mighty rivers provide valuable renewable energy, building large dams can seriously disrupt surrounding ecosystems.
example2_ja: 尽管大河能提供宝贵的可再生能源，修建大型水坝仍可能严重扰乱周边生态系统。
collocations: mighty river｜大河 ; mighty empire｜强大的帝国 ; mighty effort｜极大的努力
tip_ja: 形容词常带文学色彩；副词义“很”较口语化。

meanings_ja: n. 鸦片
definition_en: An addictive substance from poppies, used to produce certain painkillers
example1_en: The museum guide explained how opium affected trade.
example1_ja: 博物馆讲解员介绍了鸦片如何影响贸易。
example2_en: Historical research shows that the opium trade had lasting economic and social consequences for several countries.
example2_ja: 历史研究表明，鸦片贸易给多个国家带来了长期的经济和社会影响。
collocations: opium poppy｜罂粟 ; opium trade｜鸦片贸易 ; opium addiction｜鸦片成瘾
tip_ja: 不可数名词，专指鸦片，不泛指所有麻醉剂。

meanings_ja: n. 隼；猎鹰
definition_en: a hunting bird with pointed wings and a curved beak
example1_en: A falcon circled above the cliffs this morning.
example1_ja: 今天早晨，一只隼在悬崖上方盘旋。
example2_en: Protecting cliff habitats can help falcon populations recover in regions where suitable nesting sites have disappeared.
example2_ja: 在适宜巢址已经消失的地区，保护悬崖栖息地有助于隼的种群恢复。
collocations: peregrine falcon｜游隼 ; falcon nest｜隼巢 ; falcon population｜隼的种群
tip_ja: falcon指隼，不宜与泛指鹰的hawk完全等同。

meanings_ja: v. 抵制购买；拒绝参加 | n. 抵制行动
definition_en: Refuse to buy or participate in something as a protest. | An organized refusal to buy or participate as a protest.
example1_en: Local shoppers decided to boycott the store over unfair wages.
example1_ja: 当地购物者因工资待遇不公而决定抵制这家商店。
example2_en: A consumer boycott can pressure companies to improve working conditions throughout their international supply chains.
example2_ja: 消费者抵制行动能向企业施压，促使其改善整个国际供应链中的工作条件。
collocations: boycott a product｜抵制某产品 ; consumer boycott｜消费者抵制 ; call for a boycott｜呼吁抵制 ; boycott an event｜拒绝参加活动
tip_ja: 动词后直接接抵制对象；名词常用a boycott of。

meanings_ja: adj. 公平合理的；公正的
definition_en: fair to everyone involved, taking their different circumstances into account
example1_en: We agreed on an equitable division of household chores.
example1_ja: 我们商定了公平合理的家务分工。
example2_en: An equitable funding system would direct more resources towards schools serving disadvantaged communities.
example2_ja: 公平合理的拨款制度会将更多资源投向服务弱势社区的学校。
collocations: equitable distribution｜公平分配 ; equitable access｜公平的获取机会 ; equitable treatment｜公正待遇
tip_ja: equitable强调按情况公平，不一定是equal的均等。

meanings_ja: adj. 娇小的；小个子的 | adj. 适合小个子女性的
definition_en: describing a woman who is short and has a small build | describing clothes designed to fit shorter women
example1_en: My sister is petite and often needs shorter trousers.
example1_ja: 我姐姐身材娇小，经常需要裤腿较短的裤子。
example2_en: Clothing retailers can serve a wider range of customers by offering petite sizes alongside their standard collections.
example2_ja: 服装零售商可以在标准系列之外提供小个子尺码，以满足更多顾客的需求。
collocations: petite woman｜娇小的女性 ; petite frame｜娇小的身形 ; petite sizes｜小个子女装尺码
tip_ja: 通常形容成年女性娇小，不等于单纯“瘦”。

meanings_ja: adj. 标志性的；有代表性的
definition_en: widely recognised as representing a place, style, or idea
example1_en: We stopped to photograph the city's iconic stone bridge.
example1_ja: 我们停下来拍摄这座城市标志性的石桥。
example2_en: Preserving iconic buildings can strengthen cultural identity, although maintenance costs may place pressure on public budgets.
example2_ja: 保护标志性建筑可以增强文化认同，但维护费用可能给公共预算带来压力。
collocations: iconic landmark｜标志性地标 ; iconic design｜经典设计 ; iconic image｜标志性形象
tip_ja: 不只是“著名”，还强调鲜明的代表性和辨识度。

meanings_ja: n. 促成变化的人或事 | n. 催化剂
definition_en: A person or thing that triggers or accelerates change. | A substance that speeds up a reaction without being consumed.
example1_en: That conversation became the catalyst for our neighbourhood cleanup.
example1_ja: 那次谈话促成了我们社区的清洁行动。
example2_en: Investment in public transport can act as a catalyst for wider economic growth in disadvantaged regions.
example2_ja: 公共交通投资可以推动欠发达地区更广泛的经济增长。
collocations: a catalyst for change｜变革的推动因素 ; act as a catalyst｜起推动作用 ; a chemical catalyst｜化学催化剂
tip_ja: 比喻推动变化时常用a catalyst for。

meanings_ja: n. 果仁；谷粒 | n. 核心；要点 | n. 操作系统内核
definition_en: The edible inner part of a nut, or a grain seed. | The central or most important part of something. | The central software component that manages a computer's basic operations.
example1_en: She cracked the walnut and carefully removed the kernel.
example1_ja: 她敲开核桃，小心地取出果仁。
example2_en: Even exaggerated media reports may contain a kernel of truth that deserves further investigation by independent researchers.
example2_ja: 即使是夸大的媒体报道，也可能包含值得独立研究者进一步调查的些许事实。
collocations: corn kernel｜玉米粒 ; walnut kernel｜核桃仁 ; a kernel of truth｜些许事实 ; operating system kernel｜操作系统内核
tip_ja: kernel指壳内的仁或谷粒，不是桃子等的硬核。

meanings_ja: n. 梗概；概要
definition_en: A short account of the main points of a work.
example1_en: I read the synopsis before borrowing the novel.
example1_ja: 借这本小说之前，我先看了故事梗概。
example2_en: Students should provide a brief synopsis of their proposed research before discussing the methods they intend to use.
example2_ja: 学生在讨论拟采用的方法之前，应先简要概述计划开展的研究。
collocations: a brief synopsis｜简短概要 ; a plot synopsis｜情节梗概 ; a synopsis of the report｜报告概要
tip_ja: 复数为synopses；常用a synopsis of表示某作品的梗概。

meanings_ja: n. 镇压；压制 | n. 隐瞒；封锁 | n. 抑制；控制
definition_en: The forceful prevention of an activity or expression. | The deliberate prevention of information from becoming known. | The reduction or control of a reaction or process.
example1_en: His suppression of laughter failed when the puppy sneezed.
example1_ja: 小狗一打喷嚏，他就再也忍不住笑了。
example2_en: The suppression of public debate can weaken trust in institutions and prevent communities from addressing serious problems.
example2_ja: 压制公共讨论会削弱人们对机构的信任，并妨碍社区解决严重问题。
collocations: suppression of dissent｜压制异议 ; suppression of evidence｜隐瞒证据 ; immune suppression｜免疫抑制
tip_ja: 通常不可数；动词为suppress，注意双写pp和ss。

meanings_ja: n. 复苏；重新流行 | n. 戏剧等的重新上演
definition_en: a return to activity, strength, or popularity | a new production of a play or other older performance
example1_en: Our local market is enjoying a revival this spring.
example1_ja: 今年春天，我们当地的市场又热闹起来了。
example2_en: A revival of traditional crafts can create employment while preserving skills that might otherwise disappear.
example2_ja: 传统手工艺的复兴既能创造就业，也能保留原本可能失传的技艺。
collocations: economic revival｜经济复苏 ; a revival of interest｜兴趣的重新燃起 ; stage a revival｜重新上演
tip_ja: revival强调衰退或沉寂后重新活跃。

meanings_ja: v. 大量存在；充满
definition_en: To exist in large quantities or be very common
example1_en: Wildflowers abound in the fields behind our house each spring.
example1_ja: 每年春天，我们屋后的田野里都开满野花。
example2_en: Opportunities for renewable energy development abound in regions with consistent sunshine and strong coastal winds.
example2_ja: 在日照稳定且沿海风力强劲的地区，可再生能源的发展机会十分丰富。
collocations: opportunities abound｜机会众多 ; rumours abound｜传言四起 ; abound in wildlife｜野生动物丰富
tip_ja: 不及物动词；某地充满某物用abound in/with。

meanings_ja: v. 仔细考虑；沉思
definition_en: to think carefully about something for some time
example1_en: She pondered the menu before ordering vegetable soup.
example1_ja: 她仔细看了看菜单，才点了蔬菜汤。
example2_en: Policymakers must ponder the long-term consequences of replacing public transport services with privately operated alternatives.
example2_ja: 政策制定者必须仔细考虑用私营服务取代公共交通服务的长期后果。
collocations: ponder a question｜认真思考问题 ; ponder the implications｜仔细考虑可能的影响 ; ponder over something｜反复思量某事
tip_ja: 可直接接宾语，也可用ponder on/over。

meanings_ja: v. 注定；预定
definition_en: to determine someone's future or something's intended purpose
example1_en: Everyone thought the talented young dancer was destined for success.
example1_ja: 大家都觉得这位有天赋的年轻舞者注定会成功。
example2_en: Children from disadvantaged backgrounds are not destined to fail if they receive appropriate educational support and opportunities.
example2_ja: 如果获得适当的教育支持和机会，弱势背景的儿童并非注定会失败。
collocations: be destined to do｜注定会做 ; be destined for success｜注定成功 ; goods destined for export｜预定出口的货物
tip_ja: 几乎总用被动：be destined for或to do。

meanings_ja: v. 超过；胜过
definition_en: to be greater or better than someone or something
example1_en: Your homemade cakes surpass anything sold at our local bakery.
example1_ja: 你自制的蛋糕比我们附近面包店卖的任何蛋糕都好。
example2_en: Demand for renewable energy may surpass current forecasts as governments introduce stronger measures to reduce carbon emissions.
example2_ja: 随着各国政府采取更有力的减碳措施，可再生能源需求可能超过目前的预测。
collocations: surpass expectations｜超出预期 ; surpass a record｜打破纪录 ; surpass previous levels｜超过以往水平
tip_ja: 及物动词，直接接宾语，不加than。

meanings_ja: v. 逐渐增加；加剧 | v. 安装；固定 | v. 组织开展；发起
definition_en: To increase gradually in amount, strength, or seriousness. | To attach something firmly to a surface or support. | To organize and begin an activity, campaign, or event.
example1_en: Dirty dishes mounted up while our dishwasher was broken.
example1_ja: 洗碗机坏了，脏碗碟越积越多。
example2_en: As pressure mounts to reduce emissions, governments must expand renewable energy production and improve energy efficiency.
example2_ja: 随着减排压力不断增加，各国政府必须扩大可再生能源生产并提高能源效率。
collocations: mounting pressure｜不断增加的压力 ; mount a campaign｜发起运动 ; mount on a wall｜安装在墙上
tip_ja: mount可指压力等上升；mount a campaign指发起运动。

meanings_ja: v. 利用；使用
definition_en: To use something effectively for a particular purpose.
example1_en: We utilize the space under our stairs for storage.
example1_ja: 我们利用楼梯下的空间储物。
example2_en: Schools can utilize existing buildings more efficiently by sharing facilities with local communities after lessons.
example2_ja: 学校可以在课后与当地社区共享设施，从而更高效地利用现有建筑。
collocations: utilize resources｜利用资源 ; fully utilize｜充分利用 ; utilize available space｜利用现有空间
tip_ja: 比use正式；英式也常拼作utilise。

meanings_ja: n. 晶体管
definition_en: An electronic component that amplifies signals or switches electrical current.
example1_en: She carefully replaced the damaged transistor inside the old radio.
example1_ja: 她小心地更换了旧收音机里损坏的晶体管。
example2_en: The development of smaller transistors has enabled computers to process information faster while consuming less power.
example2_ja: 更小型晶体管的研发让计算机能够更快地处理信息，同时减少耗电。
collocations: transistor radio｜晶体管收音机 ; silicon transistor｜硅晶体管 ; transistor circuit｜晶体管电路
tip_ja: 指电子元件；transistor radio才是晶体管收音机。

meanings_ja: adj. 精美的；精致的 | adj. 极强烈的；极敏锐的
definition_en: Extremely beautiful and carefully made. | Describing a feeling or sensitivity of unusual intensity.
example1_en: She keeps an exquisite porcelain bowl on the shelf.
example1_ja: 她把一只精美的瓷碗放在架子上。
example2_en: Museums preserve exquisite examples of traditional craftsmanship, allowing future generations to appreciate their cultural and artistic value.
example2_ja: 博物馆保存传统工艺的精美作品，让后代能够欣赏其文化与艺术价值。
collocations: exquisite craftsmanship｜精湛工艺 ; exquisite beauty｜精美绝伦 ; exquisite detail｜精细的细节 ; exquisite pain｜剧痛
tip_ja: 常形容精美工艺；修饰pain时表示极其强烈。

meanings_ja: n. 堤岸；路堤
definition_en: a raised bank supporting transport routes or holding back water
example1_en: We walked along the embankment beside the swollen river.
example1_ja: 我们沿着涨水的河流旁的堤岸散步。
example2_en: Strengthening the river embankment could protect nearby homes from flooding as extreme rainfall becomes more frequent.
example2_ja: 随着极端降雨日益频繁，加固河堤可以保护附近住宅免受洪水侵袭。
collocations: river embankment｜河堤 ; railway embankment｜铁路路堤 ; build an embankment｜修筑堤岸
tip_ja: 既可指挡水的堤岸，也可指承托公路或铁路的路堤。

meanings_ja: adj. 不兼容的；不相容的 | adj. 合不来的
definition_en: unable to work or exist together successfully | too different in character to have a good relationship
example1_en: These headphones are incompatible with my old phone.
example1_ja: 这副耳机与我的旧手机不兼容。
example2_en: Rapid industrial expansion is often incompatible with efforts to protect fragile ecosystems without effective regulation.
example2_ja: 如果缺乏有效监管，工业快速扩张往往与保护脆弱生态系统的努力相冲突。
collocations: incompatible with｜与……不相容 ; mutually incompatible｜彼此不相容 ; incompatible goals｜相互冲突的目标
tip_ja: 固定搭配为incompatible with，不用incompatible to。

meanings_ja: adj. 精炼的；提纯的 | adj. 文雅的；有教养的 | adj. 改进的；更精细的
definition_en: Processed to remove unwanted substances. | Showing polite manners, good taste, and cultural awareness. | Improved through careful changes to details.
example1_en: This recipe uses honey instead of refined white sugar.
example1_ja: 这道食谱用蜂蜜代替精制白糖。
example2_en: Public health campaigns often encourage people to reduce their consumption of foods containing large amounts of refined sugar.
example2_ja: 公共卫生宣传常鼓励人们少吃含有大量精制糖的食品。
collocations: refined sugar｜精制糖 ; refined oil｜精炼油 ; refined manners｜文雅的举止 ; a refined technique｜改进的技术
tip_ja: 形容物质指提纯，形容人或举止指文雅。

meanings_ja: n. 参议院；上议院 | n. 古罗马元老院
definition_en: The upper chamber of parliament in some countries | The governing council of ancient Rome
example1_en: Our class watched the senate debate on television today.
example1_ja: 今天我们班在电视上观看了参议院的辩论。
example2_en: In some political systems, the senate reviews proposed laws and represents regional interests within the national government.
example2_ja: 在某些政治制度中，参议院审查法律提案，并在国家政府中代表地区利益。
collocations: senate election｜参议院选举 ; senate committee｜参议院委员会 ; senate debate｜参议院辩论 ; a seat in the senate｜参议院席位
tip_ja: 指特定国家的参议院时，通常写作the Senate。

meanings_ja: adj. 连贯的；条理清楚的
definition_en: Logical and clear, with parts that fit together well.
example1_en: After some practice, he gave a clear, coherent explanation.
example1_ja: 经过一些练习，他给出了清晰而有条理的解释。
example2_en: A coherent transport policy should connect investment in public services with long-term environmental and economic goals.
example2_ja: 一项协调一致的交通政策应将公共服务投资与长期环境和经济目标联系起来。
collocations: a coherent argument｜条理清楚的论证 ; a coherent explanation｜连贯清晰的解释 ; a coherent strategy｜协调一致的策略
tip_ja: 强调内容逻辑连贯；cohesive更强调各部分衔接紧密。

meanings_ja: v. 纠正；改正
definition_en: Correct something that is wrong or unsatisfactory.
example1_en: The shop quickly rectified the mistake and refunded me.
example1_ja: 商店很快纠正了错误，并给我退款。
example2_en: Local authorities must rectify weaknesses in drainage systems before increasingly heavy rainfall causes further damage.
example2_ja: 地方政府必须在日益强烈的降雨造成更多损害之前，纠正排水系统中的缺陷。
collocations: rectify an error｜纠正错误 ; rectify a problem｜解决问题 ; rectify the situation｜纠正局面
tip_ja: 正式用词，常接error、mistake、situation。

meanings_ja: adj. 上述的；前面提到的
definition_en: Already referred to earlier in a piece of writing.
example1_en: Please bring the above-mentioned documents to our next meeting.
example1_ja: 请把上述文件带到我们的下次会议上。
example2_en: The above-mentioned measures could reduce urban air pollution if local authorities provide sufficient funding and oversight.
example2_ja: 如果地方政府提供足够的资金和监管，上述措施就可能减少城市空气污染。
collocations: above-mentioned documents｜上述文件 ; above-mentioned measures｜上述措施 ; above-mentioned factors｜上述因素
tip_ja: 正式书面语，常置于名词前；写作中勿滥用。

meanings_ja: adj. 奇怪的；反常的 | adj. 酷儿的；非异性恋等的
definition_en: strange or unusual, in an old-fashioned use | describing sexual or gender identities outside heterosexual or conventional categories
example1_en: There was a queer rattling sound inside the cupboard.
example1_ja: 橱柜里传来一阵奇怪的咔嗒声。
example2_en: Museums increasingly include queer perspectives to reflect a broader range of experiences in their exhibitions.
example2_ja: 博物馆越来越多地纳入酷儿视角，以在展览中呈现更广泛的人生经历。
collocations: a queer feeling｜异样的感觉 ; a queer sound｜奇怪的声音 ; queer identity｜酷儿身份认同
tip_ja: “奇怪的”义较旧；身份义宜尊重当事人自称。

meanings_ja: adj. 航海的；船舶的
definition_en: Relating to ships, sailing, or navigation at sea
example1_en: My uncle collects old nautical maps and wooden boats.
example1_ja: 我叔叔收藏旧海图和木制小船。
example2_en: Modern nautical equipment helps crews navigate safely, but practical training remains essential for preventing accidents at sea.
example2_ja: 现代航海设备帮助船员安全航行，但实践培训对于预防海上事故仍然至关重要。
collocations: nautical mile｜海里 ; nautical chart｜海图 ; nautical equipment｜航海设备 ; nautical theme｜航海主题
tip_ja: nautical侧重航海和船舶；naval专指海军的。

meanings_ja: v. 透露；公开
definition_en: to make previously private or unknown information available
example1_en: The hotel would not disclose any details about its guests.
example1_ja: 这家酒店不愿透露住客的任何信息。
example2_en: Companies should disclose how they collect personal data so that consumers can make informed decisions.
example2_ja: 企业应公开其收集个人数据的方式，让消费者能够作出知情决定。
collocations: disclose information｜透露信息 ; disclose details｜披露细节 ; disclose something to someone｜向某人透露某事
tip_ja: 用disclose sth to sb；也可接that从句。

meanings_ja: n. 恼怒；忍无可忍
definition_en: strong annoyance caused by repeated problems or irritating behaviour
example1_en: She sighed in exasperation when the printer jammed again.
example1_ja: 打印机又卡纸了，她恼火地叹了口气。
example2_en: Repeated delays in public transport can cause widespread exasperation and reduce confidence in local authorities.
example2_ja: 公共交通反复延误会引发普遍的不满，并削弱公众对地方政府的信任。
collocations: in exasperation｜恼怒地 ; a sigh of exasperation｜恼火的叹息 ; growing exasperation｜日益加剧的恼怒
tip_ja: 表示烦到失去耐心；勿与加剧混淆。

meanings_ja: n. 不和；纷争 | n. 不和谐音
definition_en: Disagreement or conflict between people or groups. | A combination of musical sounds that clash unpleasantly.
example1_en: Arguments about chores caused discord among the flatmates.
example1_ja: 关于家务的争吵导致室友之间不和。
example2_en: Unequal access to resources can fuel social discord, particularly when communities feel excluded from political decisions.
example2_ja: 资源获取不平等会加剧社会纷争，尤其是在群体感到被排除在政治决策之外时。
collocations: social discord｜社会不和 ; sow discord｜挑拨离间 ; a source of discord｜纷争的根源 ; marital discord｜婚姻不和
tip_ja: 表示不和时通常不可数，语气比disagreement正式。

meanings_ja: adj. 包容的；兼收并蓄的 | adj. 包含全部费用的 | adj. 包括首尾在内的
definition_en: welcoming people of different backgrounds and abilities | including all relevant costs | including both the first and last points of a range
example1_en: Our inclusive dance class welcomes people of all abilities.
example1_ja: 我们的舞蹈课注重包容，欢迎各种能力水平的人参加。
example2_en: Schools should create inclusive learning environments where students with different needs can participate fully in classroom activities.
example2_ja: 学校应营造包容的学习环境，让需求不同的学生都能充分参与课堂活动。
collocations: inclusive education｜融合教育 ; an inclusive society｜包容的社会 ; inclusive of tax｜含税 ; an inclusive price｜全包价格
tip_ja: inclusive of表示“包含”；日期范围后用它表示首尾均含。

meanings_ja: n. 事件；发生的事
definition_en: Something that occurs, especially an unusual or interesting event.
example1_en: My uncle entertains us with stories of strange happenings.
example1_ja: 叔叔给我们讲各种怪事，逗我们开心。
example2_en: Local newspapers record everyday happenings that help future researchers understand how communities lived and changed.
example2_ja: 地方报纸记录日常事件，帮助后来的研究者了解社区居民的生活及其变化。
collocations: strange happenings｜怪事 ; local happenings｜当地发生的事 ; everyday happenings｜日常发生的事
tip_ja: 作名词常用复数happenings；正式事件通常用event。

meanings_ja: v. 喷涌；涌出 | v. 热情洋溢地说 | n. 喷涌；涌流
definition_en: To flow out suddenly in large amounts. | To express enthusiasm or praise in an excessive way. | A sudden, strong flow of liquid.
example1_en: Water gushed from the broken pipe beneath the sink.
example1_ja: 水从水槽下方破裂的管道里喷涌而出。
example2_en: When ageing pipes burst, clean water can gush into streets, wasting resources and disrupting local transport.
example2_ja: 老化的管道爆裂时，清水会涌上街道，浪费资源并扰乱当地交通。
collocations: gush out｜喷涌而出 ; gush from a pipe｜从管道中喷出 ; gush about something｜对某事赞不绝口 ; a gush of water｜一股涌出的水
tip_ja: 谈论人时，gush about常暗示赞美过于热情。

meanings_ja: adj. 封建的；封建制度的
definition_en: Relating to a system exchanging land for service and loyalty.
example1_en: The guide explained how feudal lords controlled this valley.
example1_ja: 导游讲解了封建领主如何控制这片山谷。
example2_en: Under the feudal system, access to land largely determined a person's social position and economic security.
example2_ja: 在封建制度下，土地的获取在很大程度上决定了个人的社会地位和经济保障。
collocations: the feudal system｜封建制度 ; a feudal lord｜封建领主 ; feudal society｜封建社会
tip_ja: 主要描述土地换取效忠与服役的历史制度。

meanings_ja: n. 散文；非韵文
definition_en: Ordinary written language, rather than poetry
example1_en: Her clear prose makes this book easy to enjoy.
example1_ja: 她清晰流畅的文笔让这本书读起来轻松愉快。
example2_en: Reading well-crafted prose can help students develop a wider vocabulary and express complex ideas more clearly.
example2_ja: 阅读精心写就的散文可以帮助学生扩大词汇量，更清晰地表达复杂观点。
collocations: in prose｜以散文形式 ; clear prose｜清晰的行文 ; prose fiction｜散文体小说 ; a prose poem｜散文诗
tip_ja: 不可数；不限于文学散文，也包括小说等非韵文。

meanings_ja: v. 精简；提高效率 | v. 使成流线型
definition_en: to make a process simpler and more efficient | to shape something to move easily through air or water
example1_en: We streamlined our morning routine to leave home earlier.
example1_ja: 我们简化了早晨的日常安排，以便早点出门。
example2_en: Hospitals can streamline appointment systems to reduce waiting times and improve access to essential care.
example2_ja: 医院可以优化预约系统，缩短等待时间，让人们更容易获得必要的医疗服务。
collocations: streamline operations｜精简运营流程 ; streamline a process｜简化流程 ; streamline administration｜精简行政管理
tip_ja: 通常作动词；“流线型的”用 streamlined。

meanings_ja: n. 方面；侧面 | n. 宝石等的切面
definition_en: One part or aspect of a complex subject. | A small flat surface on a cut stone.
example1_en: Cooking together revealed a new facet of her personality.
example1_ja: 一起做饭展现了她性格中新的一面。
example2_en: Public transport affects almost every facet of urban life, from employment opportunities to air quality.
example2_ja: 公共交通几乎影响城市生活的每个方面，从就业机会到空气质量。
collocations: a facet of life｜生活的一个方面 ; every facet｜每个方面 ; a different facet｜不同的侧面
tip_ja: 常用 a facet of，指复杂事物的一个方面。

meanings_ja: v. 漫步；闲逛 | v. 漫无边际地说 | n. 漫步；乡间散步
definition_en: to walk for pleasure without following a fixed route | to talk at length without a clear focus | a long walk for pleasure, especially in the countryside
example1_en: We rambled through the woods until it started raining.
example1_ja: 我们在树林里漫步，直到下起雨来。
example2_en: Speakers who ramble during presentations may struggle to communicate their main arguments clearly to an audience.
example2_ja: 演讲时漫无边际的人可能难以向听众清晰传达自己的主要论点。
collocations: ramble through the countryside｜在乡间漫步 ; ramble on about something｜絮絮叨叨地说某事 ; go for a ramble｜去散步
tip_ja: ramble on 常指说话冗长散漫，带不耐烦语气。

meanings_ja: n. 速度；速率
definition_en: Speed of movement, including direction in physics.
example1_en: The ball gained velocity as it rolled downhill.
example1_ja: 球向坡下滚动时速度越来越快。
example2_en: Engineers measure the velocity of flowing water to determine whether a site is suitable for generating electricity.
example2_ja: 工程师测量水流速度，以判断某处是否适合发电。
collocations: high velocity｜高速 ; constant velocity｜恒定速度 ; terminal velocity｜终端速度
tip_ja: 物理中velocity含方向，speed只表示快慢。

meanings_ja: adj. 固有的；内在的
definition_en: Belonging naturally to something, rather than coming from outside
example1_en: She values the intrinsic beauty of untreated wood.
example1_ja: 她欣赏未经加工的木材本身的美。
example2_en: Schools should encourage intrinsic motivation by helping students enjoy learning rather than focusing solely on external rewards.
example2_ja: 学校应帮助学生享受学习，培养内在动力，而不是只关注外部奖励。
collocations: intrinsic value｜内在价值 ; intrinsic motivation｜内在动力 ; intrinsic to｜为……所固有
tip_ja: intrinsic to表示“……所固有的”。

meanings_ja: v. 熄灭；扑灭 | v. 使希望等破灭；消除
definition_en: to stop a fire or flame from burning | to bring a feeling, hope, or idea to an end
example1_en: We extinguished the campfire before getting into our tents.
example1_ja: 我们在进入帐篷前扑灭了篝火。
example2_en: Prolonged unemployment can extinguish young people's hopes of achieving financial independence and securing stable housing.
example2_ja: 长期失业可能使年轻人实现经济独立和获得稳定住房的希望破灭。
collocations: extinguish a fire｜扑灭火灾 ; extinguish a flame｜熄灭火焰 ; extinguish hope｜使希望破灭
tip_ja: 及物动词；日常说扑灭也可用put out。

meanings_ja: v. 逐渐减少；逐渐缩小
definition_en: Gradually become smaller in amount, size, or number.
example1_en: Our savings dwindled while we searched for new jobs.
example1_ja: 我们找新工作期间，积蓄逐渐减少了。
example2_en: As freshwater supplies dwindle, governments must invest in efficient irrigation and encourage households to reduce unnecessary consumption.
example2_ja: 随着淡水供应逐渐减少，政府必须投资高效灌溉，并鼓励家庭减少不必要的用水。
collocations: dwindling resources｜日益减少的资源 ; dwindling numbers｜不断减少的数量 ; dwindle to nothing｜逐渐减至零
tip_ja: 不及物动词，强调逐渐减少，不能直接接宾语。

meanings_ja: n. 活塞
definition_en: a part that moves inside a cylinder in engines or pumps
example1_en: The mechanic removed a damaged piston from the engine.
example1_ja: 机修工从发动机中拆下了一个损坏的活塞。
example2_en: In a conventional engine, expanding gases push each piston, converting energy from fuel into mechanical motion.
example2_ja: 在传统发动机中，膨胀的气体推动每个活塞，将燃料的能量转化为机械运动。
collocations: piston ring｜活塞环 ; piston engine｜活塞发动机 ; piston rod｜活塞杆
tip_ja: 活塞在 cylinder（气缸）内往复运动。

meanings_ja: adv. 总是；始终如一地
definition_en: Always, or on every occasion.
example1_en: My brother invariably falls asleep during long train journeys.
example1_ja: 我哥哥每次坐长途火车都会睡着。
example2_en: In this study, participants with longer commuting times invariably reported having less time for leisure activities.
example2_ja: 在这项研究中，通勤时间较长的参与者无一例外都表示，自己的休闲时间较少。
collocations: almost invariably｜几乎总是 ; invariably lead to｜总是导致 ; invariably find｜总会发现
tip_ja: 比usually语气更强，表示每次如此，而非通常如此。

meanings_ja: v. 垄断 | v. 独占；包揽
definition_en: to control an entire market or supply of something | to use something so much that others cannot share it
example1_en: Please don't monopolize the conversation throughout dinner tonight.
example1_ja: 今晚吃饭时请别一直只顾自己说话。
example2_en: When a few large firms monopolize essential services, consumers may face higher prices and fewer choices.
example2_ja: 当少数大公司垄断基本服务时，消费者可能面临更高的价格和更少的选择。
collocations: monopolize the market｜垄断市场 ; monopolize the conversation｜独占话语权 ; monopolize someone's attention｜独占某人的注意力
tip_ja: 英式也常拼作monopolise；可指市场或注意力。

meanings_ja: adj. 终有一死的 | adj. 致命的 | n. 凡人；普通人
definition_en: unable to live forever | causing or likely to cause death | a human being who cannot live forever
example1_en: Even the strongest heroes in this story are mortal.
example1_ja: 这个故事里，即使最强大的英雄也终有一死。
example2_en: Recognising that we are mortal can encourage healthier habits and a greater appreciation of everyday life.
example2_ja: 认识到生命终有尽头，可以促使我们养成更健康的习惯，更加珍惜日常生活。
collocations: mortal wound｜致命伤 ; mortal danger｜致命危险 ; mere mortals｜普通凡人
tip_ja: mortal指凡人；死亡率用mortality，不用mortal。

meanings_ja: n. 辞职；辞职信 | n. 无奈的接受；听任
definition_en: The act or written notice of leaving a job voluntarily. | Calm acceptance of something unpleasant that seems impossible to change.
example1_en: She handed in her resignation after finding another job.
example1_ja: 她找到另一份工作后提交了辞职信。
example2_en: The resignation of experienced nurses can place additional pressure on hospitals already struggling with staff shortages.
example2_ja: 经验丰富的护士辞职，会给本已面临人员短缺的医院带来额外压力。
collocations: hand in your resignation｜提交辞职信 ; a letter of resignation｜辞职信 ; accept a resignation｜接受辞呈 ; with resignation｜无奈地
tip_ja: 辞职用resignation；另一义是无奈接受，不是反抗。

meanings_ja: adj. 得体的；圆通的
definition_en: Careful not to upset or offend people.
example1_en: Her tactful reply saved everyone from an awkward argument.
example1_ja: 她得体的回答让大家避免了一场尴尬的争论。
example2_en: Managers who provide tactful feedback can address performance problems while maintaining employees' confidence and motivation.
example2_ja: 管理者以得体的方式提供反馈，既能解决工作表现问题，也能维持员工的信心和积极性。
collocations: tactful approach｜得体的处理方式 ; tactful response｜得体的回应 ; tactful criticism｜委婉的批评
tip_ja: 强调顾及他人感受、言行得体，不是反应机敏。

meanings_ja: n. 安培（电流单位）
definition_en: a unit used to measure electric current
example1_en: This small lamp draws less than one ampere.
example1_ja: 这盏小灯的电流不到一安培。
example2_en: Students measured the current in amperes to compare the electrical requirements of different household appliances.
example2_ja: 学生们以安培为单位测量电流，以比较不同家用电器的用电需求。
collocations: electric current in amperes｜以安培计的电流 ; one ampere of current｜一安培电流
tip_ja: 符号为A；口语常缩为amp，复数加s。

meanings_ja: v. 修订；修改
definition_en: To change a document, rule, or plan to improve it.
example1_en: Please amend the booking to include one extra guest.
example1_ja: 请修改预订，增加一位客人。
example2_en: Parliament may amend existing legislation to ensure that remote workers receive the same protections as office employees.
example2_ja: 议会可能修订现行法律，确保远程工作者获得与办公室员工相同的保护。
collocations: amend a law｜修订法律 ; amend a proposal｜修改提案 ; amend a contract｜修改合同
tip_ja: 常指修改文件或法律；修理实物通常用mend。

meanings_ja: n. 小农；佃农
definition_en: a poor farmer working a small plot of land
example1_en: The painting shows a peasant carrying vegetables home.
example1_ja: 这幅画描绘了一位背着蔬菜回家的农民。
example2_en: Historically, peasant families often depended on a single harvest, making them particularly vulnerable to drought.
example2_ja: 历史上，小农家庭往往依赖一次收成，因此特别容易受到干旱的影响。
collocations: peasant farmer｜小农 ; peasant family｜农民家庭 ; peasant uprising｜农民起义
tip_ja: 多用于历史或传统农业语境；称呼他人可能带贬义。

meanings_ja: adj. 强制性的；必须的
definition_en: Required by a law or rule.
example1_en: Wearing a helmet is mandatory at this climbing centre.
example1_ja: 在这家攀岩中心，必须佩戴头盔。
example2_en: Mandatory safety training can reduce workplace accidents by ensuring that all employees understand potential risks.
example2_ja: 强制性安全培训能确保所有员工了解潜在风险，从而减少工作场所事故。
collocations: mandatory training｜强制培训 ; a mandatory requirement｜强制性要求 ; mandatory attendance｜强制出席
tip_ja: 常用于法规或制度要求；反义词为optional。

meanings_ja: n. 接任者；继任者 | n. 后继事物；替代产品
definition_en: Someone who takes over another person's job or position. | Something that replaces an earlier thing of the same kind.
example1_en: The retiring coach introduced her successor to the team.
example1_ja: 即将退休的教练向队员们介绍了她的接任者。
example2_en: A new leader should give their successor enough guidance to ensure that essential public services continue smoothly.
example2_ja: 新任领导者应为自己的接任者提供充分指导，确保基本公共服务平稳运行。
collocations: successor to｜……的接任者 ; appoint a successor｜任命接班人 ; choose a successor｜选择接任者 ; likely successor｜可能的接班人
tip_ja: 用successor to sb；不专指财产继承人。

meanings_ja: n. 范围；系列 | n. 光谱；频谱
definition_en: A range of related ideas, qualities, or possibilities | A range of colours or waves arranged by wavelength or frequency
example1_en: Our book club welcomes a wide spectrum of opinions.
example1_ja: 我们的读书会欢迎各种不同的观点。
example2_en: Universities should provide support for students across the entire spectrum of academic abilities and social backgrounds.
example2_ja: 大学应为各种学业水平和社会背景的学生提供支持。
collocations: a broad spectrum of｜广泛的各种…… ; across the spectrum｜涵盖整个范围 ; the visible spectrum｜可见光谱 ; the political spectrum｜政治光谱
tip_ja: 复数可用spectra或spectrums。

meanings_ja: n. 登记员；注册主任 | n. 专科培训医师（英国）
definition_en: An official responsible for keeping formal records. | A hospital doctor receiving advanced specialist training in Britain.
example1_en: The registrar checked our documents before the wedding ceremony.
example1_ja: 婚礼仪式开始前，登记员核查了我们的证件。
example2_en: The university registrar oversees student records and ensures that graduation requirements are consistently applied.
example2_ja: 大学注册主任管理学生档案，并确保毕业要求得到一致执行。
collocations: university registrar｜大学注册主任 ; registrar's office｜注册办公室 ; specialist registrar｜专科培训医师
tip_ja: 既可指登记官，也可指英国接受专科培训的医生。

meanings_ja: n. 庇护；避难 | n. 避难所；庇护处
definition_en: protection from danger, trouble, or bad weather | a safe place offering protection from danger or difficulty
example1_en: We took refuge under a bridge during the storm.
example1_ja: 暴风雨期间，我们躲到桥下避雨。
example2_en: Urban parks provide a refuge for wildlife as expanding cities gradually replace natural habitats with buildings.
example2_ja: 随着城市扩张，建筑逐渐取代自然栖息地，城市公园为野生动物提供了庇护所。
collocations: take refuge｜躲避；寻求庇护 ; seek refuge｜寻求庇护 ; a refuge from｜躲避……的庇护处
tip_ja: take/seek refuge in表示“在……避难”；refuge通常作名词。

meanings_ja: adj. 俗艳的；花哨的
definition_en: Too brightly coloured or heavily decorated to look attractive.
example1_en: He wore a gaudy jacket covered in shiny sequins.
example1_ja: 他穿了一件缀满亮片的花哨夹克。
example2_en: Some residents argue that gaudy decorations in historic districts undermine the visual character of traditional buildings.
example2_ja: 一些居民认为，历史街区里俗艳的装饰破坏了传统建筑的视觉风貌。
collocations: gaudy colours｜俗艳的色彩 ; gaudy decorations｜花哨的装饰 ; gaudy jewellery｜俗艳的首饰
tip_ja: 含贬义，指颜色或装饰过分抢眼，不只是鲜艳。

meanings_ja: adj. 多产的；成果丰硕的 | adj. 繁殖旺盛的
definition_en: Producing many works, results or achievements. | Producing many young, flowers, fruits or seeds.
example1_en: My aunt is a prolific painter with two studios.
example1_ja: 我姑姑是位多产的画家，拥有两间画室。
example2_en: Prolific researchers can contribute substantially to scientific progress, but publication quantity should not outweigh quality.
example2_ja: 成果丰硕的研究者能大力推动科学进步，但发表数量不应比质量更受重视。
collocations: a prolific writer｜多产作家 ; a prolific artist｜多产艺术家 ; a prolific goalscorer｜高产射手 ; a prolific breeder｜繁殖力强的动物
tip_ja: 强调产出多，不等于作品质量一定高。

meanings_ja: n. 草地；牧草地
definition_en: a field of grass, often containing wildflowers
example1_en: We spread our picnic blanket in a sunny meadow.
example1_ja: 我们在阳光明媚的草地上铺开了野餐毯。
example2_en: Protecting wildflower meadows helps maintain biodiversity by providing food and shelter for insects and birds.
example2_ja: 保护野花草地能为昆虫和鸟类提供食物与栖息地，从而有助于维持生物多样性。
collocations: wildflower meadow｜野花草地 ; hay meadow｜干草生产草地 ; alpine meadow｜高山草甸
tip_ja: meadow多指乡间草地，不是修剪整齐的lawn。

meanings_ja: v. 赫然耸现；隐约出现 | v. 逼近；即将发生 | n. 织布机
definition_en: Appear as a large, often threatening or unclear shape. | Seem likely to happen soon, causing worry. | A machine or frame used to weave cloth.
example1_en: A huge ship loomed out of the morning fog.
example1_ja: 一艘巨轮从晨雾中隐约显现。
example2_en: As water shortages loom, governments must invest in efficient irrigation and encourage households to reduce unnecessary consumption.
example2_ja: 随着缺水危机逼近，政府必须投资高效灌溉，并鼓励家庭减少不必要的用水。

example1_en: The clear photograph disproved his claim about the damage.
example1_ja: 这张清晰的照片证明他对损坏情况的说法不实。
example2_en: Researchers need reliable evidence to disprove the assumption that smaller classes always lead to better academic results.
example2_ja: 研究人员需要可靠的证据，才能推翻小班教学总能带来更好学业成绩的假设。
collocations: disprove a theory｜证伪理论 ; disprove a claim｜证明说法不实 ; disprove a hypothesis｜证伪假说
tip_ja: 不只是表示反对，而是用证据证明说法错误。

meanings_ja: adj. 极其必要的；迫切的 | n. 必须做的事；迫切需要 | adj. 祈使的
definition_en: Extremely important and needing to be done. | Something that must be done or given urgent attention. | Expressing a command or instruction in grammar.
example1_en: It is imperative to keep this medicine refrigerated.
example1_ja: 这种药必须冷藏保存。
example2_en: As urban populations grow, it is imperative that governments invest in reliable and affordable public transport.
example2_ja: 随着城市人口增长，政府迫切需要投资建设可靠且价格合理的公共交通。
collocations: it is imperative that｜……至关重要 ; imperative to act｜必须采取行动 ; moral imperative｜道义上必须做的事 ; imperative mood｜祈使语气
tip_ja: 常用It is imperative to do或that从句。

meanings_ja: n. 障碍物；阻塞 | n. 阻挠；妨碍
definition_en: Something that blocks movement or passage. | The act of deliberately preventing progress or action.
example1_en: A fallen branch caused an obstruction on the narrow path.
example1_ja: 一根掉落的树枝挡住了狭窄的小路。
example2_en: Removing unnecessary administrative procedures can reduce obstruction to the development of small businesses in rural areas.
example2_ja: 取消不必要的行政程序可以减少农村地区小企业发展面临的阻碍。
collocations: cause an obstruction｜造成阻塞 ; remove an obstruction｜清除障碍物 ; obstruction of justice｜妨碍司法
tip_ja: 实体障碍物通常可数；阻挠这一行为常不可数。

meanings_ja: v. 挖掘；开凿 | v. 发掘古迹或遗物
definition_en: to dig into ground and remove earth | to uncover ancient objects or buildings by carefully removing earth
example1_en: Workers excavated a deep hole for our new pool.
example1_ja: 工人们为我们的新游泳池挖了一个深坑。
example2_en: Archaeologists excavate ancient settlements to discover how earlier communities adapted to environmental changes and developed farming techniques.
example2_ja: 考古学家发掘古代聚落，以了解早期群体如何适应环境变化并发展耕作技术。
collocations: excavate a site｜发掘遗址 ; excavate a trench｜挖沟 ; excavate ancient remains｜发掘古代遗存
tip_ja: excavate可用于工程挖掘，也可用于考古发掘。

meanings_ja: n. 最后通牒
definition_en: a final demand threatening consequences if it is not accepted
example1_en: The coach gave us an ultimatum: attend practice or leave.
example1_ja: 教练向我们下了最后通牒：参加训练，否则离队。
example2_en: The council issued an ultimatum requiring the factory to improve waste treatment or face closure.
example2_ja: 市政委员会下达了最后通牒，要求工厂改善废物处理，否则将被关闭。
collocations: issue an ultimatum｜发出最后通牒 ; give someone an ultimatum｜向某人下最后通牒 ; reject an ultimatum｜拒绝最后通牒
tip_ja: 常用give someone an ultimatum；复数常为ultimatums。

meanings_ja: n. 复原力；抗逆力 | n. 回弹性
definition_en: The ability to recover or adapt after difficulties | The ability of a material to regain its original shape
example1_en: Her resilience helped her rebuild after the flood.
example1_ja: 她凭借坚韧的复原力在洪灾后重建了生活。
example2_en: Strong community networks can increase resilience by providing practical and emotional support during economic crises.
example2_ja: 紧密的社区网络能在经济危机期间提供实际帮助和情感支持，从而增强抗逆力。
collocations: build resilience｜培养抗逆力 ; emotional resilience｜情绪复原力 ; community resilience｜社区韧性 ; show remarkable resilience｜展现非凡的复原力
tip_ja: 通常不可数，强调受挫后的恢复与适应能力。

meanings_ja: n. 战争；作战
definition_en: The activity of fighting wars, including methods and weapons used.
example1_en: The museum shows how warfare changed over centuries.
example1_ja: 这座博物馆展示了几个世纪以来作战方式的变化。
example2_en: Modern warfare can damage essential infrastructure, leaving communities without reliable access to water and electricity.
example2_ja: 现代战争可能破坏重要基础设施，使社区无法稳定获得水电供应。
collocations: modern warfare｜现代战争 ; chemical warfare｜化学战 ; guerrilla warfare｜游击战
tip_ja: 不可数，强调作战活动或方式；war可指一场战争。

meanings_ja: n. 公开赞誉；高度评价 | v. 公开称赞；高度赞扬
definition_en: strong public praise for someone or something | to praise someone or something publicly and enthusiastically
example1_en: Her first film won acclaim at the local festival.
example1_ja: 她的首部电影在当地电影节上赢得了赞誉。
example2_en: The new public library has received widespread acclaim for its accessible design and sustainable construction.
example2_ja: 这座新公共图书馆因其无障碍设计和可持续建筑方式而广受赞誉。
collocations: critical acclaim｜评论界的赞誉 ; widespread acclaim｜广泛赞誉 ; receive acclaim｜获得赞誉 ; be acclaimed as｜被誉为
tip_ja: 名词通常不可数；动词常用be acclaimed as被誉为。

meanings_ja: adj. 即将到来的 | adj. 乐于提供信息的 | adj. 可得到的；会提供的
definition_en: Planned or expected to happen or appear soon. | Willing to give information or discuss something openly. | Available or provided when wanted or needed.
example1_en: We bought new walking boots for our forthcoming trip.
example1_ja: 我们为即将到来的旅行买了新徒步靴。
example2_en: The forthcoming report will assess whether investment in public transport has reduced urban air pollution.
example2_ja: 即将发布的报告将评估公共交通投资是否减少了城市空气污染。
collocations: a forthcoming report｜即将发布的报告 ; forthcoming elections｜即将举行的选举 ; forthcoming about something｜愿意谈论某事 ; no help was forthcoming｜未得到任何帮助
tip_ja: 不只表示“即将到来的”，也可指愿意透露信息。

meanings_ja: v. 装饰；使增色
definition_en: To make something more attractive by decorating it.
example1_en: Fresh flowers adorned every table at the family celebration.
example1_ja: 家庭庆典上，每张桌子都用鲜花装点。
example2_en: Public artworks adorn many urban spaces, making neighbourhoods more attractive and encouraging residents to explore their surroundings.
example2_ja: 公共艺术作品装点着许多城市空间，使街区更具吸引力，并鼓励居民探索周边环境。
collocations: adorn something with flowers｜用鲜花装饰某物 ; be adorned with｜装饰着 ; adorn the walls｜装点墙壁
tip_ja: 用adorn A with B表示“用B装饰A”。

meanings_ja: n. 法令；政令；裁定 | v. 颁令；裁定
definition_en: An official order issued by a ruler, government, or court. | To officially order or decide that something must happen.
example1_en: The new decree means our street stays closed tonight.
example1_ja: 新颁布的法令意味着今晚我们这条街将继续封闭。
example2_en: The government issued a decree requiring factories to treat wastewater before releasing it into rivers.
example2_ja: 政府颁布法令，要求工厂将废水处理后再排入河流。
collocations: issue a decree｜颁布法令 ; by decree｜通过法令 ; decree that｜颁令规定
tip_ja: 动词可接that从句；名词指有权威的正式命令。

meanings_ja: v. 增加；增强
definition_en: To increase something by adding to it.
example1_en: She sells homemade jam to augment her income.
example1_ja: 她出售自制果酱来增加收入。
example2_en: Digital resources can augment classroom teaching, but they should not replace meaningful interaction between teachers and students.
example2_ja: 数字资源能增强课堂教学效果，但不应取代师生之间有意义的互动。
collocations: augment income｜增加收入 ; augment existing resources｜补充现有资源 ; augment capacity｜提升能力
tip_ja: 较正式，通常作及物动词，强调通过添加来增加。

meanings_ja: n. 压迫；压制
definition_en: Cruel or unfair control that denies people freedom and rights.
example1_en: Her grandparents told stories about life under oppression.
example1_ja: 她的祖父母讲述了在压迫下生活的往事。
example2_en: Independent courts play a vital role in protecting vulnerable groups from oppression and defending basic freedoms.
example2_ja: 独立的法院在保护弱势群体免受压迫、捍卫基本自由方面发挥着重要作用。
collocations: political oppression｜政治压迫 ; resist oppression｜反抗压迫 ; freedom from oppression｜免受压迫的自由
tip_ja: 通常为不可数名词；动词是oppress。

meanings_ja: n. 码头；靠岸装卸平台
definition_en: A solid waterside platform where boats stop for loading or unloading
example1_en: We watched the ferry arrive from the stone quay.
example1_ja: 我们站在石砌码头上，看着渡船驶来。
example2_en: Converting an unused quay into a public promenade can reconnect urban residents with their waterfront.
example2_ja: 将闲置码头改造成公共步道，可以让城市居民重新亲近滨水空间。
collocations: along the quay｜沿着码头 ; moor at the quay｜在码头停泊 ; quay wall｜码头岸壁
tip_ja: 读音与key相同；通常指沿岸修建的实体码头。

meanings_ja: n. 狂热；痴迷 | n. 躁狂
definition_en: an unusually strong enthusiasm for an activity or object | a mental health state involving extreme energy and elevated mood
example1_en: A mania for collecting toy trains swept our neighbourhood.
example1_ja: 收集玩具火车的热潮席卷了我们社区。
example2_en: During episodes of mania, individuals may need professional support to manage sleep disruption and impulsive behaviour.
example2_ja: 在躁狂发作期间，患者可能需要专业支持来应对睡眠紊乱和冲动行为。
collocations: a mania for｜对……的狂热 ; an episode of mania｜一次躁狂发作 ; acute mania｜急性躁狂
tip_ja: 日常可指狂热；医学上的躁狂不等于普通兴奋。

meanings_ja: adj. 易燃的
definition_en: Able to catch fire easily.
example1_en: Keep inflammable liquids well away from the kitchen stove.
example1_ja: 把易燃液体放在远离厨房炉灶的地方。
example2_en: Factories must store inflammable materials safely to reduce fire risks and protect both workers and nearby communities.
example2_ja: 工厂必须安全储存易燃材料，以降低火灾风险并保护工人和附近社区。
collocations: inflammable materials｜易燃材料 ; inflammable liquids｜易燃液体 ; highly inflammable｜高度易燃的
tip_ja: inflammable是易燃的；不易燃用non-flammable。

meanings_ja: n. 代理人；代表 | n. 替代指标；替代物 | n. 代理服务器
definition_en: someone authorised to act or vote for another person | something used to represent or measure something else indirectly | a server that passes requests between users and other servers
example1_en: My sister acted as my proxy at the meeting.
example1_ja: 我姐姐作为我的代理人参加了会议。
example2_en: Researchers sometimes use household income as a proxy for living standards, although it provides an incomplete picture.
example2_ja: 研究人员有时用家庭收入作为生活水平的替代指标，尽管它无法反映全貌。
collocations: vote by proxy｜委托代理人投票 ; act as a proxy｜担任代理人 ; a proxy for｜……的替代指标 ; proxy server｜代理服务器
tip_ja: by proxy指通过代理人；a proxy for可指替代指标。

meanings_ja: v. 制止；限制行动 | v. 克制；抑制
definition_en: to prevent someone or something from moving or acting freely | to control a feeling, reaction, or increase
example1_en: She gently restrained the dog from chasing a squirrel.
example1_ja: 她轻轻拉住狗，不让它去追松鼠。
example2_en: Governments may use tighter lending rules to restrain excessive borrowing and reduce risks in the housing market.
example2_ja: 政府可以通过收紧贷款规定来遏制过度借贷，降低住房市场风险。
collocations: restrain someone from doing something｜阻止某人做某事 ; restrain anger｜克制愤怒 ; restrain spending｜控制支出
tip_ja: 常用restrain sb from doing，表示阻止某人做某事。

meanings_ja: n. 软骨
definition_en: Strong, flexible tissue found in joints and other body parts.
example1_en: The doctor explained that cartilage cushions my knee joint.
example1_ja: 医生解释说，软骨能缓冲我膝关节受到的冲击。
example2_en: Regular moderate exercise can support joint health, but damaged cartilage often takes a long time to heal.
example2_ja: 经常进行适度运动有助于关节健康，但受损软骨通常需要很长时间才能愈合。
collocations: damaged cartilage｜受损软骨 ; knee cartilage｜膝关节软骨 ; cartilage damage｜软骨损伤
tip_ja: 通常为不可数名词；不是骨头，而是有弹性的组织。

meanings_ja: v. 在脑海中想象 | v. 使可视化
definition_en: To form a clear picture of something in your mind. | To represent information using images, charts, or diagrams.
example1_en: Close your eyes and visualize a quiet sandy beach.
example1_ja: 闭上眼睛，想象一片宁静的沙滩。
example2_en: Digital models help residents visualize how proposed buildings will change the appearance of their neighbourhood.
example2_ja: 数字模型帮助居民想象拟建建筑将如何改变社区的面貌。
collocations: visualize a scene｜想象一个场景 ; visualize data｜将数据可视化 ; visualize the outcome｜想象结果
tip_ja: 英式也写visualise；可接名词或动名词。

meanings_ja: v. 歪曲；曲解 | v. 使变形；使失真
definition_en: to present information in a misleading or inaccurate way | to change the natural shape, appearance, or sound of something
example1_en: That edited clip distorts what I actually said.
example1_ja: 那段剪辑过的视频歪曲了我实际说的话。
example2_en: Selective reporting can distort public understanding of environmental issues and weaken support for necessary reforms.
example2_ja: 选择性报道可能歪曲公众对环境问题的理解，并削弱人们对必要改革的支持。
collocations: distort the truth｜歪曲真相 ; distort an image｜使图像变形 ; distort public perception｜扭曲公众认知
tip_ja: 既可指歪曲事实，也可指图像、声音失真。

meanings_ja: v. 体现；具体表现 | v. 包含；收录
definition_en: To clearly represent an idea, quality, or feeling. | To include something as part of a larger whole.
example1_en: These handmade bowls embody my grandmother's patience and care.
example1_ja: 这些手工碗体现了我祖母的耐心与用心。
example2_en: Public buildings should embody the values of inclusion by providing accessible spaces for people with different needs.
example2_ja: 公共建筑应为有不同需求的人提供无障碍空间，以体现包容的价值观。
collocations: embody an ideal｜体现一种理想 ; embody the spirit of｜体现……的精神 ; embody core values｜体现核心价值观
tip_ja: embody是及物动词，直接接所体现的品质或理念。

meanings_ja: v. 使着迷；使陶醉 | v. 施魔法于
definition_en: To delight someone greatly and hold their attention. | To put someone or something under a magic spell.
example1_en: The tiny garden enchanted us with its colourful butterflies.
example1_ja: 小花园里五彩斑斓的蝴蝶让我们陶醉其中。
example2_en: Traditional storytelling can enchant young audiences while introducing them to the cultural heritage of their communities.
example2_ja: 传统故事讲述既能吸引年轻观众，也能让他们了解所在社区的文化遗产。
collocations: enchant an audience｜使观众陶醉 ; be enchanted by｜被……迷住
tip_ja: 常用被动结构 be enchanted by，表示被深深吸引。

meanings_ja: n. 全部；整体
definition_en: the whole of something, with no part left out
example1_en: We watched the long film in its entirety.
example1_ja: 我们完整地看完了那部很长的电影。
example2_en: Researchers should examine the report in its entirety before drawing conclusions about the effectiveness of the programme.
example2_ja: 研究人员应完整审阅报告，再对该项目的成效作出结论。
collocations: in its entirety｜完整地 ; the entirety of｜……的全部
tip_ja: 常用 in its entirety，表示完整地、无遗漏地。

meanings_ja: n. 政治集团；联盟
definition_en: A group of countries or people acting together for shared aims.
example1_en: The councillors formed a bloc to protect local parks.
example1_ja: 这些议员组成了一个联盟，以保护当地公园。
example2_en: A regional trading bloc can strengthen members' bargaining power while reducing barriers to trade between participating countries.
example2_ja: 区域贸易集团可以增强成员的议价能力，同时降低参与国之间的贸易壁垒。
collocations: trading bloc｜贸易集团 ; political bloc｜政治集团 ; regional bloc｜区域集团 ; form a bloc｜组成联盟
tip_ja: 与block同音；bloc专指共同采取行动的集团。

meanings_ja: adj. 关乎最终利润的
definition_en: Relating to the final profit or financial outcome.
example1_en: The owner discussed bottom-line results with her accountant.
example1_ja: 店主和她的会计讨论了最终盈利情况。
example2_en: An excessive focus on bottom-line performance may discourage companies from investing in employee development.
example2_ja: 过分关注最终盈利表现可能使企业不愿投资于员工发展。
collocations: bottom-line results｜最终盈利结果 ; bottom-line performance｜最终盈利表现 ; bottom-line impact｜对最终利润的影响
tip_ja: 连字符形式常作定语；名词写bottom line。

meanings_ja: n. 鼠疫；瘟疫 | v. 不断困扰；使受折磨 | n. 大规模灾害；祸患
definition_en: A serious infectious disease, especially one caused by plague bacteria. | To cause repeated trouble or suffering. | A widespread problem or harmful invasion.
example1_en: The museum has an exhibition about plague in medieval towns.
example1_ja: 博物馆有一个关于中世纪城镇瘟疫的展览。
example2_en: Poor drainage continues to plague rapidly growing cities, increasing flood risks and threatening the health of local residents.
example2_ja: 排水不良持续困扰着快速发展的城市，增加了洪灾风险，并威胁当地居民的健康。
collocations: an outbreak of plague｜鼠疫暴发 ; be plagued by problems｜饱受问题困扰 ; a plague of locusts｜蝗灾
tip_ja: 动词常用be plagued by，表示长期反复受困扰。

meanings_ja: v. 混合；交融 | v. 交际；与人交谈
definition_en: mix together while remaining partly distinct | move around a group and talk to different people
example1_en: The smell of fresh bread mingled with roasted coffee.
example1_ja: 新鲜面包的香气与烘焙咖啡的香气交织在一起。
example2_en: Community festivals allow residents from different backgrounds to mingle, helping build trust and a stronger sense of belonging.
example2_ja: 社区节庆让不同背景的居民有机会交流，有助于建立信任并增强归属感。
collocations: mingle with｜与……混合；与……交往 ; mingle with guests｜与宾客交谈 ; mingle freely｜自由交往
tip_ja: mingle with既可指与某物混合，也可指与人交往。

meanings_ja: v. 渴望；立志
definition_en: To strongly want to achieve something important.
example1_en: My younger sister aspires to become a wildlife photographer.
example1_ja: 我妹妹立志成为一名野生动物摄影师。
example2_en: Many young people aspire to careers that offer both financial security and opportunities to contribute to society.
example2_ja: 许多年轻人向往既能提供经济保障，又能让自己为社会作贡献的职业。
collocations: aspire to do something｜立志做某事 ; aspire to greatness｜追求卓越 ; aspire to a career in medicine｜立志从医
tip_ja: aspire to do表立志做；aspire to后也可接名词。

meanings_ja: adj. 本土的；原住民的
definition_en: Originating or living naturally in a place, rather than arriving later.
example1_en: These flowers are indigenous to the valley near our village.
example1_ja: 这些花原产于我们村庄附近的山谷。
example2_en: Protecting indigenous languages helps preserve cultural knowledge that has been passed down through many generations.
example2_ja: 保护原住民语言有助于保存世代相传的文化知识。
collocations: indigenous peoples｜原住民族 ; indigenous languages｜原住民语言 ; indigenous species｜本土物种 ; indigenous to an area｜原产于某地区
tip_ja: 常用indigenous to；修饰人群时常将首字母大写。

meanings_ja: adj. 鲁莽的；不顾后果的
definition_en: Ignoring danger or the possible harmful results of an action
example1_en: Cycling downhill without brakes was a reckless thing to do.
example1_ja: 骑着没有刹车的自行车下坡是一种鲁莽的行为。
example2_en: Reckless lending by financial institutions can expose households to debts they have little realistic chance of repaying.
example2_ja: 金融机构不顾风险地放贷，可能让家庭背上几乎无力偿还的债务。
collocations: reckless driving｜鲁莽驾驶 ; reckless behaviour｜鲁莽行为 ; reckless spending｜不计后果的花钱 ; reckless disregard for safety｜对安全的肆意漠视
tip_ja: 比careless更强调明知有风险仍不顾后果。

meanings_ja: n. 焚化；焚烧
definition_en: The process of burning waste until it becomes ash.
example1_en: The hospital sends certain waste away for incineration.
example1_ja: 医院把某些废弃物送到别处焚烧处理。
example2_en: Waste incineration can generate electricity, but strict controls are needed to limit harmful emissions.
example2_ja: 垃圾焚烧可以发电，但需要严格管控以限制有害排放。
